Theorem 1: 'Given gamma_1>0, gamma_k=(-a)^k/2, a in (0,1/n), k>1, the attention matrix Ahat in ParaFormer is a polynomial graph filter'. Ahat = Softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d)) -- NON-NEGATIVE base. Distinct ParaFormers also exist: 2206.08317, 2303.00941, 2409.17746, 2412.16763, 2510.15425.

text: DERIVED from results/s2.jsonl, no new run: pivot_unsigned__at_pivots reads 0.0 at s=8/32/128/512 (0/4096 each). That is NOT a measurement of the S2 ablation, it is the semiring theorem restated. With out = v + Av + A^2 v the influence Jacobian wrt v is I+A+A^2, non-negative entrywise for non-negative A, so a softmax-routed arm CANNOT flip sign on the v-path at any s. The unsigned ablation is ZERO BY CONSTRUCTION on wrt='v' -- the exact defect that made M2 kill clause 2 unevaluable (instrument #15). G4 / CHECKLIST S2 can only be decided on wrt='x'.

DERIVED from results/s2.jsonl wrt='x', no new run: unsigned/signed log-log slopes over s=8..32 are -1.4281 and +0.2025; the two curves CROSS at s = 18.4. Unsigned is 3.889x BETTER than signed at s=8 (0.1025391 vs 0.0263672), 2.466x WORSE at s=32, 20.4x worse at s=128, and 0/4096 by s=512. The published '>=42.7x at s=512' separation is 0.03125 divided by the ONE-SIDED 95% Clopper-Pearson upper on 0/4096 = 0.00073111; the TWO-SIDED 97.5% upper is 0.00090020, giving 34.7x. Both bounds should be stated, not one.

COSTING, not a claim: scale/negation_scope.py is a COMPLETE M3 instrument whose absolute bar is already RED-tested (results/iter04_m3_bar_calibration.txt: predict_the_mean 1.000000, payload_only 1.414204, oracle 0.000000). It has NO ARMS -- no softmax arm, no pivot arm, bootstrap_ci has zero callers (house-events.jsonl:1926, Chase RED). The gap between M2's statistic and M3's capability is a readout head and an Adam loop, not a GPU. Nobody in this project has ever timed a training run on this CPU.

DERIVED, structural: NEITHER placement can decide the claim on its own. wrt='v' (results/m2.jsonl) has the routing comparison -- pivot_signed vs dense_signed -- but its signedness ablation pivot_unsigned__at_pivots is 0.0 by the semiring theorem, so signedness is untestable there. wrt='x' (results/s2.jsonl) has the signedness comparison -- pivot_signed__x vs pivot_unsigned__x -- but has NO dense control at all, so routing is untestable there. The claim sentence needs BOTH legs and no single placement supplies both. A dense_signed__x arm is the missing cell.

RECOMPUTED from results/s2.jsonl. (a) unsigned x-decay '-1.598, R2 0.9962' REPRODUCES EXACTLY -- but only over s=8..128, the three NONZERO points; s=512 is 0/4096 and cannot be logged. The decay is therefore fit over a 16x range, not the 64x it reads as. Substituting the one-sided CP upper for the zero gives -1.2466, R2 0.9474 over the full 8..512. Both should be stated. (b) I could NOT reproduce 'signed holds -0.021'; least-squares log-log over the same four points gives +0.0124 with R2 = 0.0204. R2 of 0.02 means the SIGN of that slope is not determined by the data. Both readings agree the arm is flat; neither licenses a signed slope value.

R5 PRE-REGISTRATION FROZEN. Appended to DONE.md BEFORE any R5 number existed (arm-building nurse still running, zero results seen). LOCK R5 d8491f67bf6b. Four kill clauses K1-K4, each with its structural-fire argument. K3 is the one that inherits instrument #15: on a v-path readout the unsigned ablation is 0 by the semiring theorem (results/s2.jsonl, 0/4096 at s=8/32/128/512) and CANNOT fire; it is evaluable only on an x-path readout, where unsigned reads 0.1025390625 at s=8. K4 exists because float('nan') >= 1.0 is False in Python.

CREDIT WHERE DUE, then a discrepancy. scale/pivot_probe.py:184-193 ALREADY documents in code what I derived independently: the v-path unsigned arm is 'vacuous, not a win' and x is 'the only channel on which signed-routed vs unsigned-routed is a real comparison'. So the S2/G4 defect was known to whoever wrote that comment. BUT the same comment cites 'the repo's record: 0.025391 / 0.009766 / 0.000000' for softmax on wrt='x' at s=8/32/128, and results/s2.jsonl reads 0.102539 / 0.014160 / 0.001221 for pivot_unsigned__x at the same sizes. 13/512 vs 420/4096 -- a 4x disagreement at s=8, far outside binomial noise. Probable cause: different arms (dense hop2 A@A vs pivot hop2 A[:,P]@A[P,:]) at different draw counts, but README.md:232 and pivot_probe.py:192 cite them interchangeably as 'softmax'. NOT called a bug; called UNRECONCILED. The load-bearing 'unsigned is ~4x better at s=8' rests on whichever of the two is the right arm, and nobody has said which.

CONSEQUENCE of the above: the wrt='x' channel has NO dense control of either sign at 4096 draws. results/s2.jsonl holds only pivot_signed__x and pivot_unsigned__x. So on the only channel where signedness is testable, ROUTING is untested; and on the channel where routing is tested (wrt='v', results/m2.jsonl), signedness is vacuous. Two arms are missing from the 2x2: dense_signed__x and dense_unsigned__x at matched n.

text: INSTRUMENT #15 IS ALIVE AND UNFIXED, in a sibling of the function that was patched. scale/m2_units.py:316 reads `k2 = (b > -0.3) if b == b else False`. That is character-for-character the bug that _verdict()'s own docstring (m2_units.py:234-236) says was ELIMINATED. b is slope(pivot_signed__not_in_P), which is NaN because loglog_slope (pivot_probe.py:70-72) returns nan when fewer than 2 points have y>0, and not_in_P is 0/4096 at every size. So NaN -> k2=False -> line 320 prints 'control decays as the mechanism requires' -> line 322 prints M2 = GREEN. tests/chase/test_m2_verdict_nan.py imports only _verdict, never report(), so nothing catches it. THE FIXED FUNCTION IS NOT THE ONE THE FULL VERDICT PATH CALLS. m2_units.py is on my do-not-touch list; reporting, not fixing.

WORSE THAN A FALSE GREEN: scale/s2_units.py:131-139. sl from loglog_slope can be NaN; `nan > -0.3` is False at line 131, so control falls to the else at 136 and PRINTS 'unsigned routing DECAYS (slope nan) while signed routing is flat (+0.0270) -- signedness is load-bearing ON TOP of routing, and that combination is the unoccupied cell.' That is the strongest sentence in the project, emitted for an undefined slope. grep -rn s2_units tests/ = zero hits; no test exercises this branch. s2_units.py is on my do-not-touch list; reporting, not fixing.

M3's THREE KILL CLAUSES CANNOT FIRE TODAY -- none of the three quantities is computed by any code in the repo. negation_scope.main() calls only calibrate_bar; bootstrap_ci has zero callers; no unsigned-arm NRMSE exists anywhere. tests/chase/test_checklist_kills_are_evaluable.py runs 5 FAILED / 1 PASSED, and the one that passes (test_g4_has_an_evaluator) passes because its evaluator is s2_units.report -- the site with the NaN defect above. CAVEAT I AM PUTTING ON MY OWN NUMBER. tests/chase/test_m2_instrument_binds.py reports 4 of 5 FAILED, including '|P| = 6 not 8 at s=8' and 's=8 pivot/dense cells are bitwise-identical'. results/m2.jsonl confirms the latter: pivot_signed__in_P/s8 and dense_signed__at_pivots/s8 both read exactly 0.024658203125. So at s=8 the pivot restriction is nearly vacuous (6 pivots over at most 7 causal rows). My DERIVED crossover of s=18.4 between signed and unsigned on wrt='x' is anchored on the s=8 endpoint and is therefore SOFT. The bracket that survives is measured, not fitted: unsigned is above signed at s=8 and below it at s=32, so the crossover lies in [8,32]. The value 18.4 should be quoted as an interpolation, never as a measurement.

THE TRADEOFF REFUSED, WITH ARITHMETIC. [RUN, my own probe, 20 torch threads, CPU] one fwd+bwd of the M3 shape (causal signed op + pivot hop2 + readout, d_model=16, k=8) costs 146.1 ms/step at n=128 s=260, so 616 steps fit in a 90 s bucket; 275.9 ms at n=256 s=260; 482.1 ms at n=128 s=512; 1605.2 ms at n=256 s=512. Warm-up step excluded and DECLARED; 5-step median; no optimizer, no eval, no bootstrap, so this is a LOWER BOUND on a full arm, not the arm cost. A 3-arm 500-step comparison at s=260/d=256 is ~3 buckets, ~220 s. [DERIVED from meta.seconds in results/m2.jsonl + results/s2.jsonl] the statistic already cost 4895.8 s + 1558.2 s = 6454.0 s = 107.6 min of this same CPU, of which 5049.4 s = 84.2 min is the s>=1024 columns alone. So the CAPABILITY route is roughly 3% of what the STATISTIC route has already spent. The premise that the decisive route is the expensive one is false on this box.

INSTRUMENT #15, THIRD INSTANCE -- AND IT IS IN M4, A MANDATORY CHECKLIST CELL. [RUN] `python -m pytest tests/chase/test_checklist_kills_are_evaluable.py -x -q -k m4` -> 1 failed in 1.41s. AssertionError: 'the perturbed token was outside `keep` in all 8 draws' (assert 0 > 0), tests/chase/test_checklist_kills_are_evaluable.py:104. The mechanism is in the call signature itself: ev.lowest_salience_token(x, RHO, exclude=keep) EXCLUDES the keep set, so the token that gets perturbed can never be inside keep, so the measured movement of kept content is 0.000000e+00 BY CONSTRUCTION. M4's kill is 'max change > 1e-12'; that quantity is never nonzero, so M4's kill CANNOT FIRE. The headline 'do(c) measured at 0.000000e+00 for eviction against 2.154868e-05 for post-softmax gating' (CHECKLIST.md:153,182; README.md:825,853) is therefore not a comparison of two operators -- one side is a structural constant. This also removes M4 as the zero-training fallback capability I was about to nominate.

CORRECTION TO A NUMBER I WAS GIVEN AND WOULD HAVE REPEATED. BLiMP sentential_negation_npi_scope, arXiv:1912.00582v4 Table 4, extracted from the PDF with pypdf: '5-gram 45, LSTM 23, TXL 53, GPT-2 73, Human 81'. My brief carried GPT-2 = 95. IT IS 73. Four of the five anchors were correct, which is exactly what made the fifth easy to miss -- the same internally-consistent-externally-wrong pattern that produced fifteen instrument failures here. Consequence: the paradigm is NOT saturated. GPT-2-large is 774M params and sits 8 points BELOW the human 81, and Transformer-XL (103M params, 103M training tokens) reads 53. A 25.7M model has a real band to land in, and the honest target for a small-data run is TXL's 53, not a near-ceiling 95.

BabyLM STRICT-SMALL IS THE WRONG TRACK FOR THIS MODEL, with arithmetic. Strict-Small = 9.96M WORDS (arXiv:2504.08165 Table 1, 'Total - 9.96M 98.04M 100%'); Strict = 98.04M words. This project's tokenizer is byte-level (vocab_size=256, ceq/hf/train.py DEFAULTS), so 9.96M words x 5-6 bytes = 49.8-59.8M byte-tokens. Chinchilla for 25,182,208 non-embedding params at 20 tok/param = 503,644,160 tokens. Strict-Small is SHORT BY 8.4x-10.1x and would need 8.4-10.1 epochs; Strict is 490-588M tokens = 97-117% of the budget. Also verified independently: instantiating ceq/hf/train.py DEFAULTS reproduces 25,707,520 params exactly (25,182,208 non-embedding + 131,072 + 262,144 + 1,024 + 131,072). Also: arXiv:2404.06214 is the 2nd-challenge CALL FOR PAPERS, not a findings paper -- it has no corpus table. The findings papers are 2504.08165 and 2412.05149.

BLiMP EVALUATION IS ALMOST FREE, and that is what makes it a candidate. Protocol (arXiv:1912.00582): zero-shot minimal-pair likelihood comparison, no fine-tuning, no generation -- 'observing whether they assign a higher probability to the acceptable sentence'. 1,000 pairs per paradigm, so sentential_negation_npi_scope is 2,000 forward passes. At 2*N*tokens forward-only with ~71 byte-tokens/sentence: 7.301e12 FLOPs = 73-730 CPU-seconds depending on assumed throughput (10/50/100 GFLOPS, ESTIMATE, not sourced). The full 67-paradigm suite is ~67x that. The COST IS ALL IN THE PRETRAINING, none in the eval. ALSO NOTE: arXiv:2504.08165 reports NO wall-clock and NO GPU type for any BabyLM baseline or entrant -- grepped, zero hits. There is no published compute figure to compare against.

REFINING MY OWN M4 FINDING -- being precise, because the loose version overstates it. [READ] tests/w3/test_w3_eviction.py:84-92: BOTH arms perturb the SAME token (`crushed`, chosen with exclude=keep) and compare settle_gated vs settle_evicted on the same edit. So the eviction-vs-gating comparison IS symmetric and fair, and the gating leak of 2.154868e-05 is a real measurement. What is NOT a measurement is the eviction side: the crushed token is excluded from keep, so settle_evicted drops it entirely, so editing it cannot move kept rows -- 0.000000e+00 is 'you deleted it, so it stopped mattering', a tautology. The defect is in the KILL, not the comparison: CHECKLIST M4's kill reads 'max change > 1e-12' about SETTLED STATE OF UNRELATED CONTENT, i.e. content inside keep, and tests/chase/test_checklist_kills_are_evaluable.py:104 shows the perturbed token was outside keep in 8 of 8 draws (assert 0 > 0, FAILED). So the M4 kill is written about kept content and measured on deleted content, and it cannot fire. Corrected reading: M4's claim survives as a systems statement (exact retraction), but its pre-registered kill is unevaluable as coded.

R5 LEARNABILITY CONTROL -- RUN, and it is the control R5 needs before any arm is credited. [RUN, CPU, 20 threads] M3 negation-scope at s=260, d=256 (flipper@3, payload@258, query@259), n_train=1024, held-out batch generated with a DIFFERENT seed (999 vs 0). An ORACLE-GATHER model -- routing handed over for free, 6,337 params, only the multiplicative combination learned -- reads: steps=0 heldout 1.0009 [ABOVE BAR], steps=100 heldout 0.0478, steps=300 heldout 0.0139, steps=500 heldout 0.0071, in 3.86 SECONDS total for the 500-step run. TWO THINGS THIS ESTABLISHES. (1) RED-FIRST FIRES: the untrained model reads 1.0009, above the predict-the-mean bar of 1.0, so K1 can reach both sides of its threshold -- unlike M2 clause 2 and unlike the M4 kill. (2) The readout+MLP+Adam budget SOLVES this task in under 4 seconds when routing is free, so any arm failure at d=256 is attributable to ROUTING and not to the training budget. The oracle-routed upper bound is 0.0071 against a predict-the-mean 1.0; that is the band the arms have to land in.

THE 25,707,520 FIGURE IS WRONG BY 20,480 AND THE CAUSE IS A BUG IN sizing.py. [RUN] building the notebook's exact object via ceq.hf.train.build(**dict(ceq_train.DEFAULTS)) and summing p.numel() gives 25,728,000, not 25,707,520. [READ] ceq/sizing.py:128-140 `per_layer = (3*d*d + d*d) + (d*f + f*d) + 4*d` counts qkv/o_proj correctly as bias-free (modeling_ceq.py:393-394 use bias=False) but the MLP at modeling_ceq.py:419 is nn.Linear(d,f) / nn.Linear(f,d) with PyTorch's DEFAULT bias=True, and sizing.params() never adds those bias vectors. 8 layers x (2048+512) = 20,480, matching the diff EXACTLY. Magnitude 0.08% -- does not move the T4 memory conclusion (preflight reproduces README's 2.72 GiB / 13.50 GiB budget / +10.78 GiB headroom) -- but it is the arithmetic every scaling claim in this project is built on.

THE 1.6% CHINCHILLA CLAIM HOLDS UNDER EVERY CONVENTION. [RUN] notebook ships steps=2000 (colab/train_ceq.ipynb:191), batch=8, seq=512 (ceq/hf/train.py:45-46) = 8,192,000 tokens. Against 20*N: 1.593% at the claimed 25,707,520, 1.592% at the measured 25,728,000, 1.627% at sizing.py's own non-embedding convention of 25,182,208 (TOKENS_PER_PARAM=20 at sizing.py:275, chinchilla_tokens uses non-embedding at sizing.py:289-290). All three round to 1.6%. The 300M pricing also reproduces from code: CFG_300M non-embedding 302,088,192, h_softmax 41.4/46.8 A100-h, h_sgate 129.7/257.2 A100-h at seq 1024/2048 -- NOT fabricated in prose.

CAVEAT ON A NUMBER MY OWN NURSE PRODUCED, and the contamination is MINE. The 25.7M model was timed on this CPU at min 4454.2 ms/step, median 6799.9 ms/step, batch 8 seq 512, 20 torch threads. Steps 2-4 climbed from 6.8s to 9.3s -- I was running my own R5 cost probe and the M3 learnability control on the same box at the same time. Treat 4454.2 ms as the best-case and the median as contaminated BY ME. Separately: the two T4 extrapolations DISAGREE BY 4-9x -- 6ND at 65 TFLOPS and 25-40% MFU gives 24-39 ms/step, while measured-CPU divided by an UNVERIFIED 20-40x speedup guess gives 111-223 ms/step. Neither is a T4 measurement and neither should be quoted as one. Also worth knowing: ceq/sizing.py:304-307's own docstring says gpu_hours() is 'only meaningful for the SOFTMAX arm'; the sgate cost is the softmax number times MEASURED_STEP_RATIO = {1024: 3.13, 2048: 5.49}, a hardcoded dict at tests/chase/test_scale_sizing.py:494 measured on an RTX 4060 Laptop, not on an A100.

NEW MEASUREMENT, one bucket, 40.8 s total, no file written to results/. Ran scale.pivot_probe.run_arm at the SHIPPED protocol (n_draws=4096, k=8, placement='in_P', seed=0, protocol='SCALING', wrt='x') at the missing size s=16. pivot_unsigned__x/s16 = 174/4096 = 0.042480469, CP95 [0.036510, 0.049114], 18.5 s. pivot_signed__x/s16 = 119/4096 = 0.029052734, CP95 [0.024125, 0.034666], 22.3 s. THE INTERVALS DO NOT OVERLAP: at s=16 the UNSIGNED arm is significantly BETTER than the signed one. Combined with unsigned 0.014160 vs signed 0.034912 at s=32, the crossover is bracketed by MEASUREMENT in (16, 32) and interpolates to s = 19.6 (log-log slopes over 16..32: unsigned -1.5850, signed +0.2651). This replaces my earlier s=18.4, which was anchored on s=8 where |P|=6 makes the pivot restriction nearly vacuous. The bracket is now measured on a size where that objection does not apply, and the answer barely moved. STANDING CONSEQUENCE: 'softmax cannot do this' is false below roughly twenty tokens of context, with non-overlapping intervals saying so.

SECOND CORRECTION TO MY OWN BRIEF. 'TinyStories publishes GPT-4-graded scores at 1M/2.5M/8.3M/28M' is TRUE only of ANECDOTES. arXiv:2305.07759 Figures 6, 7 and 8 are SINGLE-PROMPT, SINGLE-SCORE examples (e.g. 28M reads Grammar/Creativity/Consistency 9/6/9 on the 'ladder' prompt, 9/7/9 on 'pumpkin', 8/5/8 on 'black cat'; 1M reads 6/3/2, 4/4/3, 2/1/1). The paper's ACTUAL benchmark protocol is Section 3: '~50 prompts', '10 completions with temperature 1', averaged -- and that averaged result appears ONLY in Figure 4, a bar-chart IMAGE keyed by hidden-size x layer-count, NOT by the four round parameter labels. There is no text table of averaged scores at 1M/2.5M/8.3M/28M. Anyone citing those four as a benchmark is citing three anecdotes. Also: the paper's largest sweep point is ~80M ('almost perfect scores in terms of grammar and consistency'), not 28M.

TINYSTORIES PARAMETER BRANDING DOES NOT SURVIVE A COUNT. Instantiating each live HuggingFace config.json as GPTNeoForCausalLM: TinyStories-1M has 3,745,984 parameters at its config's literal vocab_size=50257. Re-counting at vocab_size=10000 (the paper's stated 'top 10K most common tokens') gives 1,169,536 / 3,125,504 / 9,396,736 / 31,376,384 / 37,596,672 / 24,932,352 for the six checkpoints. The paper's footnote 2 says the models are '1M/3M/9M/28M/33M'; the live repo says '1M/3M/8M/28M/33M'; the prose says 8.3M. UNVERIFIED which convention the branding counts. CONSEQUENCE FOR BRACKETING: this project's 3,652,096-param run is bracketed by (2.5M, 8.3M) and the 25.7M notebook default by (8.3M, 28M) -- TWO DIFFERENT PAIRS, not one. And every TinyStories checkpoint uses a 50,257 BPE vocab while this project is byte-level (vocab 256), so parameter-count bracketing does not imply comparability.

TINYSTORIES COSTED. Dataset: 2,141,709 rows, TinyStories-train.txt = 1,924,281,556 bytes (HTTP HEAD on the CDN). Token count is NOT stated in the paper; measured by tokenizing a real 20MB sample with tiktoken gpt2 = 4.098 bytes/token, giving ~469.6M tokens as a LOWER BOUND (the paper's 10K-vocab restriction splits rare words further, so the true count is higher). Training 25.7M params on one epoch: 6*N*D = 7.2432e16 FLOPs; on a T4 at 65 TFLOPS fp16 (nvidia.com spec, quoted) at 10/20/30% MFU = 3.10 / 1.55 / 1.03 hours. FITS A 12-HOUR SESSION WITH ROOM FOR THREE EPOCHS at the pessimistic MFU. Paper's own hardware statement, Section 4 verbatim: 'All of the models can be trained on a single V100 GPU within at most 30 hours.' GRADING IS NOT FREE: 50 prompts x 10 completions = 500 GPT-4 calls, measured at 389 input / 73 output tokens per call from the paper's own worked example = $8.03 on gpt-4-0613, $0.68 on gpt-4.1. THE FREE SUBSTITUTE EXISTS AND THE PAPER USES IT: held-out cross-entropy on TinyStories-valid.txt, which Section 3.1 says tracks the GPT-4 scores -- but the correlation is stated QUALITATIVELY ONLY, with no regression and no mapping, so it cannot be converted into a graded score. No eval harness was ever released; only Evaluation_prompts.yaml (45 entries).

text: THE MISSING ARM IS MEASURED AND IT GOES AGAINST THE ROUTING STORY AT SMALL s. [RUN, 143.9 s total, shipped protocol n_draws=4096 k=8 placement=in_P seed=0 SCALING wrt='x', nothing written to results/] dense_signed__x: s=8 243/4096 = 0.059326172 CP95[0.052286,0.067003]; s=16 190/4096 = 0.046386719 CP95[0.040149,0.053281]; s=32 169/4096 = 0.041259766 CP95[0.035376,0.047809]. Against pivot_signed__x re-measured in the same process: 0.026367188 CP95[0.021679,0.031747] / 0.029052734 CP95[0.024125,0.034666] / 0.034912109 CP95[0.029503,0.040997] -- and the s=8 and s=32 values REPRODUCE results/s2.jsonl BIT-FOR-BIT, so the instrument did not move. VERDICT: on the representation path DENSE BEATS PIVOT AT EVERY SIZE MEASURED, with NON-OVERLAPPING intervals at s=8 and s=16. Routing does not buy anything below s=32 on this channel. Log-log slopes over 8..32: dense -0.2620, pivot +0.2025 -- dense decays only a third as fast as it does on the v-path (-0.746), and the two curves CONVERGE rather than separate.

PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION, WRITTEN BEFORE THE RUN. Extrapolating the two log-log fits above, pivot_signed__x overtakes dense_signed__x at s = 46. The cheapest possible test is ONE size: s=64, both arms, same protocol, ~100 s of CPU. THE READING IS FIXED NOW. (A) pivot > dense at s=64 with non-overlapping CP95 -> routing is vindicated on the representation path and the convergence at s<=32 is a small-s artifact. (B) intervals OVERLAP at s=64 -> the crossover is real but slower than fitted; report the overlap, do not round it into a win. (C) dense STILL above pivot at s=64 with non-overlapping CP95 -> the extrapolation is wrong, routing does not help on the representation path in the measured range, and the claim sentence may not say routing holds signed influence flat WITHOUT naming the channel it fails on. I am running it next; this text does not get edited afterwards.

M2' R1-R4 are ONE mechanism. On the SAME 512 draws at s=128/512, R2's sign-determinacy predicate PARTITIONS M2's flip statistic: flip|determined 0.0068 CP[0.0014,0.0199] vs flip|undetermined 0.1622 CP[0.0867,0.2661], intervals disjoint, 24x. R2 GREEN IS M2's flip rate going to zero.

R2's determined fraction is a DOMINANCE TEST ON THE ONE-HOP EDGE, not a sign-structure test. Closed form: determined iff |A[i,j]| >= the one-sided pivot mass. Measured D_block 0.8555/0.8438 at s=128/512 while all-signs-agree is only 0.0215/0.0508. The 10^4 resamples reproduce the closed form exactly and buy nothing; at s=512 they OVER-report determinacy 55/64 vs the exact 53/64.

THE TWIN TEST: on |A| (scale/s2_probe.py absmag, magnitudes bit-identical, signs stripped) R2's determined fraction is 1.0000 and R3's balanced-ambiguity is exactly 0.0000 at s=128 and s=512, n=512. Both criteria are maximally passed by an operator with NO SIGNS. Neither can be evidence for signed influence.

R1's kill cannot fire: perturbing an off-support token moves the pivot readout by 0.000e+00, 96/96 bitwise identical at s=128 and s=512. Same structural zero as M2 clause 2. On dense_signed the same probe reads 8.795e-02 / 5.201e-02, so the kill fires only if the pivot mechanism is abandoned.

A crossing cannot be located where the parameter is non-injective and the function undefined. Instrument #15's NaN-slope-read-as-GREEN, rebuilt.

ROOT CAUSE, one sentence: all four M2' routes are thresholds on ONE scalar -- the intervened token's two-hop path weight against the one-hop offset and the background spread -- which is sign-blind (measured) and degree-1 homogeneous under per-row rescale (the rescale lemma), so no one of them can distinguish signed influence from magnitude bookkeeping.

R5 COST CORRECTION -- THE PIVOT ARM IS BOTTLENECKED BY A PYTHON LOOP, NOT BY THE OPERATOR. [READ] scale/m3_capability.py:100-107: hop2 = torch.stack([pivot_hop2(a[i], select_pivots(k[i], k_pivots)) for i in range(n)], dim=0). My own shape probe using a SHARED pivot set taken from batch element 0 ran the same operator at 146.1 ms/step at n=128, s=260. So the gap is the loop, and it is vectorizable (batched gather + bmm). ANYONE COSTING R5 SHOULD PRICE THE VECTORIZED FORM, NOT THIS ONE.

Two things are NOT yet established and must not be assumed: no arm has been run at d >= 256 to completion, and the pivot arms have not been run at n_train=1024 to completion. R5 is not GREEN, it is not RED, it is PARTIALLY RUN, and the part that has run says the arms do not clear the absolute bar.

THE SUCCESSOR, NAMED IN ADVANCE AS THE STANDING ORDER REQUIRES. If K1 holds at d >= 256 once the pivot arms are vectorised and run, R5 does not leave the project with nothing -- the successor is TinyStories at the 25.7M notebook default, and it is costed: 6*N*D = 7.2432e16 FLOPs for one epoch over ~469.6M measured tokens, 1.03-3.58 T4-hours at 10-30% MFU, fitting one free 12-hour session with room for three epochs at the pessimistic MFU. The published points 8.3M and 28M bracket 25.7M. THE GRADING IS THE CATCH AND IT HAS A FREE SUBSTITUTE: GPT-4 grading is 500 calls at $0.68-$8.03, but arXiv:2305.07759 Section 3.1 uses held-out cross-entropy on TinyStories-valid.txt as its own proxy -- qualitative correlation only, no regression, so it cannot be converted into a graded score and must be reported as loss, not as a score. BabyLM/BLiMP is the WEAKER successor for this model: strict-small is 8.4-10.1x too small for a Chinchilla budget at 25.7M, so the right track is Strict (98.04M words), and the honest target is Transformer-XL's 53 on sentential_negation_npi_scope, not GPT-2's 73 and certainly not the 95 my brief carried.

text: it.0 METHODS.md written. SUPERMARTINGALE PROPERTY HOLDS for the grid mixture — proven two ways in §2. Direct: conditional expectation is linear over a finite sum, each term is a single-lambda supermartingale, w_k>=0 preserves each inequality. Reframe: the mixture IS a single predictable-lambda process with lambar_{t-1} = posterior mean of lambda; Ebar_t = Prod(1 + lambar_{i-1} d_i/B) exactly. Not an extension of the predictable-lambda result, a SPECIAL CASE of it. Ville threshold 20 = 1/0.05 exactly. §1.4 repair is NOT fiction.

it.0 BUT THE CONSTRUCTION HAS A LIVE BREAK, and it is B. d_i = NRMSE_twin - NRMSE_settled. NRMSE = RMSE/std(y) is UNBOUNDED ABOVE. Repo record: 2.1166 at n_train=128 and 1.3165 at 512 (CHECKLIST.md:333), seed-mean 1.007076 at 2048 (CHECKLIST.md:868), 5.8198 OOD (ceq/nash.py:4). B=1.0 from the absolute bar is WRONG — the 1.0 bar is a CREDIT rule on the SEED-MEAN at the end, it bounds no individual arm. If |d_i|>B ever occurs a factor goes NEGATIVE, nonnegativity dies, Ville does not apply, every anytime-valid claim in the round is VOID — and the printout looks normal.

it.0 RULE 5 REROUTE for B. Clipping d_i post-hoc does NOT repair it — clipping d up at -B raises the conditional mean and H0 IS a statement about that mean. Repair that works: clip the OUTCOME in the DEFINITION, before any data. d_i = min(NRMSE_twin,C) - min(NRMSE_settled,C), B=C, recommend C=2.0. Legitimate because it defines a new bounded outcome variable a priori; min(.,C) is monotone so per-seed sign never flips; and the round already refuses credit above 1.0 so the clipped scale and the claimable scale agree everywhere the claim may live. Assertion |d_i|<=B must VOID the process, never clamp. Fallback if C not agreed: sign(d_i) in {-1,0,+1}, B=1 — bounded by construction, but discards magnitude and is sprt.py territory.

it.0 THREE MORE CONDITIONS, each invisible in the output when violated. (1) lam_i predictable — automatic under the mixture, which is a reason to prefer it. (2) prior weights w_k CONSTANT — posterior weights move and are supposed to, feeding them back as new priors kills the telescoping identity and there is no theorem left. (3) NO outcome-dependent seed exclusion — dropping a seed for how it came out makes the indicator F_i-measurable not F_{i-1}-measurable and E[I_i d_i|F_{i-1}]<=0 does not follow. The existing NRMSE>=1.0 gate does NOT trip this: it filters CELLS on the seed-mean at the end, not d_i within a cell. Applying the same threshold PER SEED would break the process. Two readings of one number, differing by everything.

it.0 ALPHA BUDGET, unresolved and Chase must pin it before the first seed. Two directions each rejecting at 20 spends alpha=0.05 EACH; two-sided family-wise rate is bounded by 0.10, not 0.05. it.0 FLIESS / CARLYLE-PAZ: **FIELD, NOT COMMUTATIVE RING.** The contract asked and the answer is decisive. Berstel-Reutenauer, Noncommutative Rational Series with Applications, Ch.2 §1: p.27 opens `We start by assuming that K is a commutative ring.` Then p.30, marginal 643, IMMEDIATELY BEFORE the Definition of rank and the Definition of the Hankel matrix: `We suppose from now on that K is a field.` **The hypothesis switches EXACTLY at the definition of rank.** Thm 1.6 (Carlyle and Paz 1971, Fliess 1974a) p.31 verbatim: `The rank of a formal series S is equal to the codimension of its syntactic right ideal, and is equal to the rank of its Hankel matrix.` — carries NO hypothesis of its own, INHERITS the field. Confirmed independently: Balle-Mohri CAI 2015 Thm 1 (Fliess) verbatim `Let S be a field. Then, the rank of the Hankel matrix Hf associated to a function f : Sigma* -> S is finite if and only if f is rational. In that case, there exists a WFA A representing f with rank(Hf) states and no WFA representing f admits fewer states.` Their §3 preamble: `From here on, we will assume that the semiring S is in fact a field. This enables us to define the rank of a matrix.`

it.0 HOW FAR IT ACTUALLY GENERALISES, and it is sideways not upward. NOT to commutative rings — to DIVISION rings. Sakarovitch, Handbook of Weighted Automata Ch.4 draft 19-Sep-2008, §5.2 p.50 verbatim: `We now suppose that K is a field, not necessarily commutative, hence a skew field, or division ring.` Thm 15 p.50: `A series s over A* with coefficients in a division ring is recognisable if and only its rank is finite.` (sic, `if and only its`). OVER SEMIRINGS RANK IS REPLACED, not weakened: Berstel-Reutenauer Ch.1 Prop 5.1 p.11 uses `stable finitely generated left K-submodule` instead, and the Notes p.25 say verbatim `taken from Jacob (1975) who extends to semirings a Hankel-like property given by Fliess (1974a) for fields.` Labai-Makowsky arXiv:1512.02430 §4 p.6 verbatim: `notions of orthogonality, rank, and norms do not readily transfer to the semiring setting.`

it.0 AND THE PID CASE IS AN OPEN PROBLEM, stated as such in print. Berstel-Reutenauer Ch.7 §1 p.121, Thm 1.1 (Fliess 1974a), hypothesis `Let K be a commutative principal ring and let F be its quotient field` — verbatim `Let S in K<<A>> be a series which is rational of rank n over F. Then S is rational over K and has a linear representation over K of dimension n.` NOTE: **the rank is taken over the QUOTIENT FIELD F, then realised over K.** Load-bearing proof step p.122: `mu(K<A>) is a submodule of a free K-module of rank n, hence is also free and has rank <= n` — that is submodule-of-free-is-free, which needs a PID and FAILS over a general commutative ring. And van Heerdt/Kupke/Rot/Silva, FoSSaCS 2020, arXiv:1911.04404v2 p.16 verbatim: `The second part of Lemma 23 would follow from a PID variant of Fliess' theorem [12]. **We are not aware of such a result, and leave this for future work.**` Also Berstel-Reutenauer Ex 5.5 p.24: S = Sum n*a^n IS recognizable over N but the smallest stable N-submodule is NOT finitely generated.

Ville 1939 REACHED IN FULL (numdam.org, Etude critique de la notion de collectif, Gauthier-Villars). **THEOREME 1, printed p.84, verbatim: `Soit {s_n} une suite definissant une martingale et lambda un nombre > 1. Nous avons l inegalite Pr. { B. sup._(n) s_n(X_1, X_2, ..., X_n) >= lambda } <= 1/lambda.`** HYPOTHESIS AS PRINTED: his condition (14) is `s_0 = 1` AND a conditional-expectation **EQUALITY** — a MARTINGALE, not a supermartingale — and lambda > 1. So the form this round uses (SUPERmartingale, E[M_0] <= 1) is NOT Ville 1939 Theoreme 1 verbatim. The supermartingale form is Wang-Ramdas arXiv:2304.01163v3 §2.1 p.4 eq.(3) `P[sup_{0<=n<inf} M_n >= C] <= C^{-1} E[M_0]`, and Durrett V5 Exercise 4.8.2 `P(sup X_n > lambda) <= EX_0/lambda`. METHODS.md now cites the modern form and says why. My §1 proof is self-contained optional stopping so it never depended on the citation.

The chain family's recursion z' = a z + b is a 2-dimensional linear recursion in (z, 1), so over a finite alphabet its Hankel has ring-weighted-automaton rank exactly 2 -- the SAME rank as the plain counter, whose t* is 1. claim: the pivot family (twin/settled/argmax cells) demotes token s-2 from the value path to the weight path: pivots exclude (0, s-1) and every attention row is tril(-1)-strict, so no pivot row can place x[s-2] on the value path; b[s-2] and a[s-2] reach the readout only through softmax-weight nonlinearities (gate, pivot s-2's own query, pivot selection). At t*=1 the label is a[s-1]*b[s-2], concentrated on exactly the demoted token, and every label term at every t* carries the invisible factor a[s-2]. The softmax cell keeps s-2 on the value path directly. The e3_t1/t2 softmax-vs-pivot deficit is therefore confounded by construction, not evidence about settling.
consequence: MOVE 1: new cells with the exclusion lifted -- exclude=(0,) so p=s-1 is a legal pivot (av[s-1] equals the softmax cell's own row, so softmax becomes an interior point of the twin's function class), and/or inclusive-diagonal pivot rows (j<=p). Falsifier, ~25 min box: e3_t1 n_train=2048 seed 0; if twin-plus does not close at least half the 0.103 gap to softmax, the exclusion is not the binding term and the deficit is optimization; if it closes and settled-plus still equals twin-plus, settling retires on clean ground.

claim: the settled cell iterates the mixture weights alpha inside an 8-simplex, which is a reparameterisation within the twin's own output family {alpha @ av}; the solve can reallocate but cannot add. Literature: softmax attention is already the one-step-converged update of a fixed-point iteration (modern Hopfield, exponentially small retrieval error in one update); iterating the normalisation to its fixed point (Sinkformer) yields only small gains; DEQ-class fixed points at best match explicit nets; gains from iteration appear when the iterated object is the token representation (looped/weight-tied blocks), i.e. depth. Own numbers agree: settled-twin = +0.002190 at t*=2; settling adds sd 3.874x and no mean; at t*=8 train NRMSE 0.860972 sits on the 2-hop ceiling 0.866025 while eval reads 1.112208 -- the arm memorises noise because the 2-hop term is a 3-way product no depth-1 linear-mixing readout represents (log k depth for k-hop composition).
corroboration: Ramsauer et al. arXiv:2008.02217 (attention = Hopfield update, converges in one update); Sander et al. arXiv:2110.11773 (Sinkformer); Bai et al. arXiv:1909.01377 (DEQ); Yang et al. arXiv:2311.12424 (looped transformers); Sanford-Hsu-Telgarsky arXiv:2402.09268 (hop_k: depth floor(log2 k)+2 suffices, Omega(log k) conditional lower bound, empirically depth 4 solves k<=4); Marion et al. arXiv:2410.01537 + Duranthon et al. arXiv:2509.21936 (softmax Bayes-optimal on single-location regression, linear attention strictly short -- e3_t1 is a single-location task); Tarzanagh et al. arXiv:2306.13596 (softmax GD converges to max-margin token selection)
consequence: MOVE 2: iterate the representation, not alpha -- a weight-tied looped cell x_{t+1} = x + A(x_t) @ x_t (input-injected, 4769 params unchanged), 3 loops. Credit-clean on e3 per LOOP_PROMPT 1.7d because softmax-looped vs softmax involves no signed resolvent. Falsifier, ~40 min box: e3_t2 + e3_t8, n_train=2048, seed 0, steps 150 and 600; if looped-3 neither beats single softmax at t*=2 nor goes below 1.0 at t*=8, depth-via-loop dies on this corpus and the twin ships on its earned +0.111396 with the softmax loss as headline.

verdict: softmax wins here for three reasons that are now separable: (1) a construction confound -- the pivot family excludes the freshest token from the value path (F1); (2) the fixed point solves the wrong unknown -- weight-space, not representation-space, and one-step softmax is already a converged fixed-point step (F2); (3) at t*>=8 nobody is within reach of their own ceiling because multi-hop terms are products needing depth ~log2(t*), and every arm has depth 1. The equilibrium thesis is not yet refuted -- it has not yet been aimed at the representation. Two moves, both with kill switches under an hour of box time, before any ladder money.

Hypergeometric: P(miss a c=12 cluster) = 1 - C(295,10)/C(307,10) = 0.6671. It DID miss: 0 of 12 drawn, and 0 of the 31 tests/foreman/ KEEP rows (P of that = 0.3392). A uniform draw needs k=67 to reach 95 percent on c=12. Deeper: KEEP 307 carries 46 distinct classing rules; the draw touches 7, leaving 39 rules and 151 of 307 rows (49.2 percent) unsampled, and 10 of the 16 multi-row rule strata (122 rows) get zero draws. Errors here are rule-generated, so path-uniform sampling does not sample rules. SETTLING MEASUREMENT: tests/mars/test_spotcheck_draw_is_powered_against_clustered_error.py, 3 failed 1 passed. NOT A HIT: the presumption axis is fine -- all 36 PRESUMED rows are ATTIC, zero are KEEP, and 5 of 40 ATTIC with only 4 non-presumed gives P(>=1 presumed drawn) = 1.0000. REPLACEMENT ROUTE: stratified_allocation() in that same file -- floor 1 per rule stratum with n>=2 (16 strata), singletons pooled, remainder proportional; budget 30 KEEP. Buys P(detect a wholly-wrong rule) = 1.0000 for ALL 46 rules vs 0.1862 worst case for uniform-30, and P(detect the measured cluster) = 1.0000 vs 0.3329 shipped. HONEST LIMIT: against a c=12 cluster placed adversarially in the largest stratum (n=114) stratification is WORSE than uniform at matched budget (0.4951 vs 0.7157); it buys total rule coverage, not fixed-size-cluster power. SATURN verdict should be caveated, not discarded.

name: cost-model-15.95x-decomposition
detail: 12391/777 = 15.95x, closed exactly by four MEASURED factors. Model unit reconstructed as flat: 12391/8 = 1548.875 s/point and 17 x 1548.875 = 7.31 h, inside the quoted 6.7-7.7 h band, which identifies a single per-point scalar with NO size term. A MARKUP U/anchor-mean 719.58s = 2.152x (inflates). B ANCHOR anchor-mean / the same 6-run point on this machine 112.2s = 6.413x (inflates). C STRUCTURE 6-run point / 2-run rho point = 2.727x, splitting as seeds 3/2 = 1.500x times arm-amortization (sm+sg)/sg = 1.818x (inflates). D SIZE measured 777s / flat-at-small 329.2s = 2.360x (DEFLATES). 2.152 x 6.413 x 2.727 / 2.360 = 15.95x. THE 8x-vs-3.85x DOCSTRING ERROR CONTRIBUTED ZERO of the overage -- the model was flat, so it carried no size term to be wrong. It is unspent, not unpaid: 8 / 3.851 = 2.08x on the next estimate that carries one, and the depth axis L=2..16 is that estimate.

name: sgate-cost-diverges-from-softmax-on-the-two-300M-axes
detail: At IDENTICAL parameter count (3,319,296 confirmed at H=4, H=8, H=16) sgate goes 1.000 -> 1.392 -> 3.076 RE while softmax goes 0.818 -> 0.834 -> 0.940 RE. With tokens/step pinned at 4096, seq 128->1024 takes sgate 1.000 -> 5.525 RE against softmax 0.818 -> 1.167 RE. So on the two axes a 300M run multiplies hardest, the operator costs 3.3x (heads) and 4.7x (seq) its own control in wall-clock, at equal or near-equal parameters. A parameter-count cost model is structurally blind to both. MODEL_CARD.md's shipped wall-clock 1.32x is a 3.3M seq-128 H-4 number and does not transfer.

POINT: cheapest crosser (steps=2400, n_train=8192, t*=8) at NRMSE 0.93. FRONTIER t*=8 n*(150)=never, n*(600)=32768, n*(2400)=8192, n*(9600)=2048; t*=32 never/never/32768/8192. Basis: gate (b) static local decoder already reads t8=0.756967 and t32=0.731839 on ~2048 rows while the trained softmax arm sits at 1.131993 and 1.163365 at n_train=2048 -- a sample/optimisation gap, not an information ceiling; rho axis (parity worse at 12.8M than 3.3M at every rho) says capacity is not binding. name: scale/vram_gate.py::require -- prices VRAM for a CPU-only job
finding: require() returned FITS on 7162 MiB FREE VRAM while the job it was gating, scale/r10_capacity_sweep.py, spends ZERO VRAM (m3_capability.py is CPU-only by construction) and 4275.1 MiB of HOST RSS against 6.2 GiB free host RAM. The gate is GREEN on a resource the job does not touch and BLIND to the one that actually binds it: three concurrent n=32768 seats would need 12.8 GiB host and the gate would pass all three. Same shape as the aggregate-occupancy failure the module was written for, one layer over.

text: OPEN REGION DISCHARGED AT t*=8, UNDECIDED AT t*=32. 48 cells, all blocks bar-CALIBRATED. Best at n=32768/150: t*=2 0.8748 LEARNS, t*=8 0.9724 LEARNS, t*=32 1.0061 NO READING. First crossing measured in the t*>hop region; the OPEN-REGION PROTOCOL no longer covers t*=8.

F-1 STEPS HURT, DATA HELPS, MONOTONE IN BOTH. At n=2048 every block degrades 150->9600 steps: t*=2 0.9714->1.6871, t*=8 1.1285->2.2541, t*=32 1.1582->2.2384. Every crossing in the grid is at the SHORTEST rung (150). A budget spent on steps instead of examples would have concluded the region unlearnable and been wrong.

F-2 THE 1-HOP CEILING RISES TOWARD THE BAR: sqrt((t*-1)/t*) = 0.7071, 0.9354, 0.9843 at t*=2,8,32. At t*=32 a PERFECT one-hop model has 0.0157 margin under predict-the-mean. This is the multi-hop architectural case in closed form, emitted to the journal before the first cell ran (r10_capacity_sweep.py:146).

OPEN, BINDING: every n=32768 cell is seed 0 -- --seed-cap restricts later seeds to smaller rungs, so the two per-block replicates are bit-identical duplicates (determinism check, not variance). t*=8 clears the bar by 0.0276 and t*=32 misses by 0.0061 against a measured seed range of 0.0345 at n=2048. Both decisive readings sit INSIDE the seed spread. Seeds 1-3 at n=32768 dispatched.

SELF-STRIKE x2. (1) Claimed the t*=32 cell was starved and could not start, inferred from falling free memory; the process table showed both seats already running and allocating -- a resource reading used as proxy for a job state readable directly. (2) Called the ceiling the analytic floor on the TASK; it is the floor imposed by softmax hop budget 1. Corrected reading is F-2 and is stronger.

INSTANCE 16 OF THE ROUND MECHANISM, and the costliest. Script it.11 gates the open-region verdict on "N=8 SEED CI excluding 1.0 (bootstrap B=1e4)". r10_capacity_sweep.py:101 computes bootstrap_ci(pe, y_eval, seed=seed) -- resampling EVAL EXAMPLES within one trained model. Every cell therefore ships boot_lo/boot_hi that answer "is this model below 1.0 on this eval set", not "does a random training run land below 1.0". t*=8 n=32768 ships [0.9641,0.9814], which excludes 1.0, so a reader checking the shipped field concludes it.11 is satisfied by seed 0 alone. It is not: N=1. The proxy is biased flattering -- CI width 0.0173 against a measured seed range of 0.0345 at n=2048, understating uncertainty by ~2x. A CI over the wrong population standing in for the CI the pre-registered rule names.

INSTRUMENT PROPERTY, measured, bounded. r10_capacity_sweep is deterministic given (seed, threads) but NOT across thread counts. t*=8 n=2048 seed=0 ran twice at threads=8 and threads=6: eval 1.1285342332 vs 1.1280431664, drift 4.91e-4 from float reduction order alone. Both n=32768 seed=0 rows ran at threads=12 and are bit-identical to 10 dp. CONSEQUENCE, stated so it is not overclaimed: the 48-cell grid was swept at mixed thread counts (8,6,6,12,12), so same-table cells carry ~5e-4 comparability drift -- 1000x L-VALUE (5e-7), but 12x SMALLER than the t*=32 margin above the bar (0.0061) and 56x smaller than the t*=8 margin below it (0.0276). No verdict in the table turns on it. It does mean a bit-identical duplicate confirms determinism AT FIXED THREADS, not reproducibility, and any future L-VALUE comparison across these cells fails on thread count alone.

name: scale/r10_capacity_sweep.py::t32 -- softmax NO READING in every affordable cell
finding: t*=32 cleared the NRMSE<1.0 bar in ZERO of the 7 cells run. Best 1.006066 at (150 steps, n=32768), bootstrap [1.0033,1.0094] -- above the bar and above the 1-hop analytic ceiling 0.984251. Per C-D this is UNTESTED, not refuted: no CEQ arm result at t*=32 means anything until something crosses. The n-trend 1.1537 -> 1.0272 -> 1.0061 across n=2048/8192/32768 at 150 steps is monotone toward the bar and unresolved at the affordable frontier.

name: scale/r10_capacity_sweep.py::steps-axis-is-an-overfitting-axis at n=2048
finding: At n_train=2048 every additional training step makes the HELD-OUT reading worse, at every t*. t*=8 seed 0: train NRMSE 0.866/0.560/0.302/0.125 against eval 1.129/1.497/1.920/2.254 at 150/600/2400/9600 steps. The arm memorises 2048 examples; the generalisation gap grows monotonically to +2.13. The 9600-step corner the stake statement names is therefore not a capability probe at this n, and a grid that spends its budget on the steps axis buys overfitting. The frontier moves with n ONLY.

text: SELF-STRIKE. Instance 16 was filed implying the round table rested on the eval-example CI. MERCURY marked every single-seed cell n=1, computed N=8 seed CIs at (150,2048) where seeds existed, and stated the n=32768 seeds were priced and not bought. The instrument hazard is real; the attribution was not. Corrected in R10_MECHANISM.md rather than edited away.

INSTANCE 17, caught before it fired, committed by HOUSE in the SCHEDULER. Two queued jobs both waited on the predicate "no r10_capacity_sweep process is running": seeds 4-7 (4.3 GiB) and the it.10 octave at n=65536 (7.9 GiB extrapolated). Both wake on the same edge when seeds 1-3 end, and the octave preflights BEFORE the sibling allocates, so it passes the gate on free memory that is already spoken for. 4.3 + 7.9 = 12.2 GiB on a 16.1 GiB box. Occupancy NOW is a surface proxy for will-there-be-room; a sibling that has not allocated yet is invisible to it, which is the sentence vram_gate.py:19 already contains -- "no per-job gate can see aggregate occupancy" -- re-committed one layer up in the thing scheduling the gated jobs. Repaired by an explicit dependency on the seeds job completion line rather than on occupancy. No collision occurred; the octave was stopped and re-queued before either woke.

SELF-STRIKE, caught by JUPITER. HOUSE quoted the cross-thread noise floor as 4.911e-4 twice, and derived from it that t*=32 margin above the bar is 12x the drift and no verdict turns on it. There are THREE cross-thread pairs, not one: t*=2 2.345e-3, t*=8 4.911e-4, t*=32 7.311e-6. Max is 2.345e-3, 4.8x the quoted figure; t*=32 margin 6.066e-3 is 2.59x that floor, not 12x. A single measurement was presented as a population statistic -- the identical shape to the N=1 seed defect HOUSE was concurrently objecting to, committed in the sentence objecting to it. Verified independently before accepting the correction.

it.10 FRONTIER. Crossing n* at steps=150: t*=2 BELOW the grid (0.952349 at n=2048, not extrapolated backwards); t*=8 n*~16238 (log2 13.99) INTERPOLATED between measured 8192 and 32768; t*=32 n*~48823 (log2 15.58) EXTRAPOLATED 0.575 octaves past the grid on a single segment, no bracketing cell. Isotonic assumption HELD with max violation exactly 0.0 in all 9 sequences, so the fit is the IDENTITY MAP and every crossing comes from linear interpolation in log2(n), not from the regression -- stated rather than presented as work. Steps axis: dNRMSE/dsteps POSITIVE in 12 of 12 adjacent pairs across 6 of 6 eligible cells, smallest delta +0.087107, largest +0.646806, all 33x-276x the noise floor; n=32768 has only steps=150 and is NOT MEASURED on that axis. Backend sklearn 1.9.0 with a separately-named PAVA fallback asserted against it on a genuinely violating sequence.

t*=32 CANNOT BE ANSWERED FROM THE MEASURED CELLS. The margin being extrapolated to zero is 6.066e-3, only 2.59x the 2.345e-3 noise floor. The curve DECELERATES measurably: per-2-octave drop 0.126566 -> 0.021089, ratio 0.167. Continued geometrically it ASYMPTOTES AT 1.00185 AND NEVER CROSSES, and that asymptote gap to the bar (1.85e-3) is BELOW the noise floor. n*~48823 is therefore best read as a lower bound conditional on a crossing existing at all. The single cell that settles it: t*=32, n_train=65536, steps=150, ~2x the n=32768 wall time.

Perron-weighted sup (the repo own formalised norm): holds 7/7 where defined, UNDEFINED on 5/12 from reducible P_II, reported null and never as a pass, and is 1-2 orders looser than the degree-weighted norm. AMENDMENT STATED NOT APPLIED SILENTLY: err(t) <= lambda_2^t needs the phrase in the degree-weighted 2-norm to be true.

DUAL ORACLE max disagreement 9.992007e-16 against an IMPORTED 1e-10 tolerance (kirchhoff.py:98-106, not re-picked); Kirchhoff third route 2.220446e-16 on the |B|=2 path family and the same against the closed form u_x = 1 - x/(L+1). SELF-STRIKE: AUTOMATION LAUNDERED A WRONG ANSWER. The R10_MECHANISM.md instance-count note went stale twice because a literal string replacement silently failed -- the sentence wraps across a line break, so the match never fired and no error was raised. It was then rewritten to DERIVE the count by scanning the file, on the reasoning that a derived number cannot go stale. The derivation matched the row pattern across the WHOLE document, picked up a second table further down, and published 'twenty-two times' for a file holding twenty. Scoping the scan to the one section fixed it: 14 table rows + 6 instance sections = 20. THE LESSON IS NOT 'check your regex'. Replacing a hand-maintained number with a computation felt like a correctness improvement and was not; it changed a number that could be wrong into a number that could be wrong AND carried the authority of having been computed. Deriving a value is not the same as deriving it over the right region. Filed against the same mechanism as instance 20 (an instrument's scope not matching its claim) rather than as a new instance, because the catalogue counts MECHANISMS and this is that mechanism again, not a new one. Documented in place, in the paragraph it corrupted.

THE DUAL ORACLE IS ONLY DUAL WHERE IT DOES NOT MATTER MOST. The two routes agree to 1.554e-15 max over 29 instances and reject an absorbing-side deg+1 plant 29/29 (gaps 2.916667e-01 to 6.301520e-01, median 0.4831) and a Kirchhoff-side plant 17/17. But the SHARED plant -- deg+1 applied to BOTH routes -- is rejected 0/17, max gap 3.331e-16. Reason: I - Q = D^-1 L_T is a DIAGONAL relation, so the routes share adjacency and degrees. What the 29/29 agreement licenses is normalisation, indexing, block structure and transposition conventions; what it does NOT license is the shared graph data. A corruption of the graph itself passes both oracles silently. STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCE, named as required: the absorbing route solves nonsymmetric I - P_II on the interior alone and reads u directly; the Kirchhoff route solves symmetric unnormalised L on interior + {b} against e_b and recovers each value as the RATIO z_v/z_b, tied to literal spanning-forest counts (8/13, 7/13, 4/13) by brute-force enumeration at 0.000000e+00.

IT.15 DUAL ORACLE COUNTS, four categories not three. 31 instances (28 rungs + 3 probes): 29 passed, 0 failed, 0 errored, 2 INAPPLICABLE, 29 dual-checked. A FOURTH category surfaced and is counted separately: 1 NEVER GENERATED (widen-n128-d4, seed 0x3a150000 -- bisection stepped from above 0.905 to 0.8943072442 with no integer |B| in band). It is emitted under its own kind; a dict-merge that filed it back under kind=rung was found and fixed at scale/r10_dual_oracle.py:578. Max disagreement 1.554312e-15 on reproduce-n1024-d4-t0.95, min 1.110223e-16, against a tolerance IMPORTED as kirchhoff.AGREEMENT_TOL from scale/kirchhoff.py:106 -- demo() asserts OBJECT IDENTITY so a local re-pick fails the self-check. Single-route check alongside: sum_b omega^(b) = 1, max deviation 2.220446e-15. INAPPLICABLE reported as UNCHECKED not passes: |B|=1 (cofactor ratio is 0/0) and a two-component graph with one boundary node per component (every grounding singular), both dual_checked=false; a third probe on the same ring with |B|=2 passes, so the refusals are not a broken route. Zero of the 28 drawn rungs are inapplicable, which is WHY the probes exist. Weight positivity is UNTESTED, NOT SATISFIED -- kirchhoff.laplacian builds unit conductances only.

HALT DEMONSTRATED LITERALLY, and the band clustering CONFIRMED against it.14. Halt: same 3-instance corpus clean emits 3 rows; with deg+1 planted on instance 1 it emits 0 rows and raises CorpusHalted, gap 3.980916e-01 -- the two instances that passed their OWN check are not emitted, which is what 'disagreement halts the corpus, not the reading' has to mean. CLUSTERING REPRODUCED EXACTLY: 12/12 rungs in [0.9434514476, 0.9499393658], all in the top [0.94,0.95) bin, 121 eigensolves, lambda_2 delta 0.0 against results/r10_it14_corpus_spec.jsonl with identical boundary sizes. So the corpus does not cover the band it claims -- it covers the TOP FIFTH. Widening (one argument, hi = target against a pre-declared ladder) gives 16 rungs spanning [0.9033, 0.9450], 3-4 per bin. PRICED: 1 band miss in 17 attempts, eigensolves per rung unchanged (9.7 vs 10.1), but 64% MORE second-oracle work per rung (44.2 vs 27.0 Kirchhoff solves) because lower targets need larger |B|.

SELF-STRIKE: THREE STATIC-ANALYSIS LEADS FORWARDED TO SATURN, ALL THREE FALSE POSITIVES. The 'unknown import symbol' on scale/r10_corpus_spec.py was the analyzer failing on an UNTRACKED file -- the module resolves and exports every name used, and SATURN's reproduce_check proves the generator was IMPORTED not reconstructed at delta 0.0. The two arity hits were a starred-unpack the analyzer cannot count through. This is the second time this round HOUSE forwarded linter output as candidate defects and it did not hold: JUPITER's 'redeclared isofit' was likewise a guarded except-ImportError fallback. Both times the leads were labelled as leads and both times they cost an agent a verification pass. A static analyzer's complaint is evidence that a HUMAN-READABLE INVARIANT MIGHT BE VIOLATED, not that one is; on an untracked or dynamically-assembled module its false-positive rate is high enough that forwarding without checking reachability is not worth the recipient's time.

IT.11 COMPLETE ACROSS ALL THREE BLOCKS AT N=8. t*=2 n=2048 LEARNABLE [0.9462, 0.9591]; t*=8 n=32768 LEARNABLE [0.9739, 0.9768]; t*=32 n=32768 NOT LEARNABLE mean 1.0034, seed CI [1.0009, 1.0057], B=10000. The t*=32 reading is a VERDICT, not a refusal: the interval lies entirely ABOVE the bar so lo > 1.0 and the pre-registered rule returns NOT LEARNABLE at full N. It agrees with JUPITER it.10 frontier analysis, which predicted the curve asymptotes at 1.00185 -- the measured interval brackets that value. SCOPE, STATED: this establishes that t*=32 does not cross AT n=32768 WITH 150 STEPS on 8 seeds. It does not establish that no amount of data would cross; the n=65536 octave that would test it was refused on memory. JUPITER deceleration measurement (per-2-octave drop 0.126566 -> 0.021089, ratio 0.167) is the evidence that it may never cross, and that remains an extrapolation, not a measurement.

THE IT.10 OCTAVE WAS REFUSED BY ITS OWN GATE, WHICH IS THE GATE WORKING. scale/vram_gate.py preflight on t*=32 n=65536: needs 9859 MiB (7888 extrapolated RSS x 1.25 contention margin), only 8808 MiB available on a 16091 MiB box. Refused at second zero rather than OOMing partway through a ~13-minute run. The wait that preceded it also behaved: 66 minutes, and it did NOT release on the two occasions occupancy read 0 sweep procs while the durable seeds-complete condition was still false -- the conjunction repair holding on live cases. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE SCIENCE: the single cell JUPITER named as settling whether t*=32 ever crosses (t*=32, n=65536, steps=150) is NOT MEASURED, and the block's verdict is therefore 'does not cross at n=32768' rather than 'does not cross'. The cell is affordable only on an otherwise-idle box: 9856 MiB free required.

THE N=8 RULE JUST PAID FOR ITSELF, MEASURABLY. t*=32 at n=32768, eight seeds: 1.006066, 1.003982, 0.997284, 0.998440, 1.003313, 1.008121, 1.006066, 1.003698. TWO OF THE EIGHT ARE BELOW THE BAR (0.997284 seed 2, 0.998440 seed 3). So a SINGLE-SEED run at this cell reports LEARNS with probability 2/8 = 25% and NO READING otherwise. The sweep happened to draw seed 0 (1.006066) and iteration 9 published NO READING; had it drawn seed 2, the same cell would have published the opposite verdict on identical code and identical data. The N=8 seed CI [1.0009, 1.0057] is entirely above the bar and the rule returns NOT LEARNABLE, correctly, because the rule asks about the MEAN and not about whether some draw crosses. This is the concrete cost of the it.9 single-seed state that --seed-cap produced, and the concrete value of buying the seeds out: at t*=8 the extra seeds CONFIRMED the original draw (seed 0 read 0.9724 against an N=8 mean of 0.9754), and at t*=32 they REVERSED nothing but showed the reading was a coin-flip away from reversing. A verdict published from one draw at this cell would have been unfalsifiable-looking and 25% wrong.

THE IT.10 OCTAVE IS UNAFFORDABLE AND A BETTER CELL IS NOT. n=65536 needs 9859 MiB against 8370 available after killing every non-essential process; the remaining consumers are Claude sessions and system processes and the gap is 1489 MiB. n=57344 also refuses at 8731. n=49152 FITS at 7603 -- and it is the MORE informative cell, not a consolation: JUPITER it.10 frontier fit put the predicted crossing at n* = 48,823, so n=49152 sits 0.7% above it and tests the prediction directly rather than extending the axis generically. LABELLED HONESTLY: 49152/32768 = 1.5x is 0.58 OCTAVES, not the one octave the script asks for, and the script wording is not satisfied by it. Running all 8 seeds so the result is it.11-admissible rather than another single draw. CAVEAT THAT LIMITS WHAT IT CAN SETTLE: JUPITER two readings of his own data predict 1.0 (linear interpolation crossing at 48823) and ~1.002 (geometric deceleration asymptoting at 1.00185) at this cell. They differ by ~0.002 against a measured cross-thread noise floor of 2.345e-3, so a SINGLE seed cannot discriminate them. An N=8 seed CI (width ~0.005 at this block) is marginal for it too. The cell is worth measuring as the first point beyond the grid; it is not expected to adjudicate between his two extrapolations and will not be reported as if it had.

THE HOST-RSS MODEL IS SUPERLINEAR AND MY LINEAR FIT WAS FLATTERING. Measured peak at n=49152 over 10 samples: 6584 MiB, against the fitted prediction 6082 from RSS = 665.5 + 0.1102*n -- an underestimate of 502 MiB (+8.2%). The per-example slope is NOT constant: 0.1102 MiB/example over 8192->32768 and 0.1409 over 32768->49152, so growth is superlinear in n and the linear model degrades exactly where it was used, at the largest rungs. RE-EXTRAPOLATED with the local slope, n=65536 needs ~8892 MiB actual and ~11115 with the 1.25 contention margin, not the 9859 the gate quoted -- so the octave is FURTHER out of reach than its refusal stated, not closer. THE ERROR DIRECTION IS THE POINT: the fit reproduced a HELD-OUT point (n=2048, 10 MiB error) and was believed on that evidence, but holding out a point INSIDE the fitted range tests interpolation and says nothing about extrapolation beyond it. A model validated only where it was fitted, then used past that range, is the same shape as every other proxy in this round's catalogue -- and it erred PERMISSIVE, quoting a smaller requirement than the truth. The gate refused anyway, which is why nothing was lost.

FIRST BEYOND-GRID CELL: t*=32, n=49152, steps=150, seed 0 reads 0.999940 -- BELOW the bar. The same seed at n=32768 read 1.006066, so a half-octave of additional data moved it 0.006126 and it crossed. This lands where JUPITER it.10 frontier fit predicted: he put the crossing at n* = 48,823 by linear interpolation in log2(n), and this cell sits 0.7% above that and reads six parts in 100,000 below 1.0. It is CONSISTENT WITH his interpolation reading and IN TENSION WITH his geometric-deceleration reading, which had the curve asymptoting at 1.00185 and never crossing. WHAT THIS IS NOT: a verdict. One seed, and a margin of 6e-5 against a measured cross-thread noise floor of 2.345e-3 -- the reading is 39x INSIDE the instrument's own resolution, so on this cell it is a coin flip. That is exactly the situation already measured one rung down, where two of eight seeds at n=32768 fell the other side of the bar and a single draw reported the opposite verdict 25% of the time. Seven more seeds are running and the it.11 gate will refuse to rule until all eight exist.

The inconsistency was visible inside single paragraphs and survived because nobody read the two halves against each other. Verified after: 0 remaining in README.md and test_m3_etasks.py, the guarded test still passes 5/5, and the producer parses. What remains is DELIBERATE: MARS's it.13 report (9), the guard describing the defect (9), SATURN's binding (1), the it.13 record (2), the binding script that computes BOTH forms to compare them (1), and one correction note. text: The it.14/15 corpus declares NO train/eval split: no split field in either .jsonl, no split rule in either report. Amendment stated, not applied quietly: the corpus must declare which instances are train and which are eval. Both partitions a reader could take were measured under a stated rule -- graph identity = SHA-256 over the sorted edge list on the generator's own node labels, labelled identity adds the boundary list and the float64 bytes of g, family membership = spec.draw_graph(n, extra_for(n, mean_deg), rng(seed)) reproduces the edge set bit-for-bit. SAME GRAPH FAMILY: yes on both splits, 40/40 instances regenerate bit-for-bit, out_of_family empty. SHARED GRAPHS: SPLIT-ARM (reproduce|widen) = 0, disjoint seed bases 0x3a140000+i against 0x3a150000+i. SPLIT-FILE (it14|it15) = 12, and all 12 are labelled-identical, so 4412 of 10105 eval interior rows (43.66%) carry a label already present in train. Not automatically fatal and the cost is stated: arm reproduce IS it.14's corpus by design -- the same reproduction that made it.15's second oracle trustworthy (max_lambda_2_delta 0.0) is what makes the two files an unusable split -- and a leaked label inflates eval rather than destroying it, so it fails toward the optimistic side, the opposite end from impact's train 4.93e-08 / eval 1.478 where nothing leaked and cos(w0,w1) = -1.077e-08 made transfer impossible. Same disease, opposite ends: the split does not separate what a consumer can memorise. The third reading, 'graph in x', is NOT ANSWERABLE: the corpus ships adj/boundary/g and declares no tensorisation, so it is recorded as an open precondition, not a pass. SHOWN ABLE TO FAIL: a planted leak (one train instance copied into eval) reads shared_graphs=1 status=failed; a planted 32-node ring reads same_graph_family=false status=failed; the clean SPLIT-ARM control does NOT fire. All three asserted in demo().

text: Bar IMPORTED BY OBJECT IDENTITY: FAIL_BAR = rips_gate.FAIL_BAR, value 0.9, scale/rips_gate.py:61, declared there as 'the decoder is doing essentially nothing' and already used for exactly this anti-triviality role at scale/impact.py:1121 ('FAIL_BAR 0.9, must be >=0.9'). demo() step 0 asserts the identity so a local re-pick fails the self-check. Feature ladder declared before any number was read, four rungs, all static and strictly local: F0 degree; F1 + ball sizes r=1,2,3; F2 + boundary-neighbour count, hop-to-B, 1/(1+hop); F3 + gbar = (1/deg) sum of g over boundary neighbours. Fit is rips_gate.fit_eval, half/half held out, rows shuffled by PROBE_SEED 0x3a160000; both halves from the SAME instance or the SAME arm -- within-split, not transfer. HELD-OUT NRMSE over 28 rungs: F0 median 1.0066, 0/28 at or under 0.9. F1 median 1.0060, 0/28. F2 median 1.0192, 0/28. F3 median 0.7639, min 0.5670, 25/28 AT OR UNDER 0.9. Pooled within-split: reproduce 0.7961, widen 0.7975, both failed. Reported plainly rather than hunting a probe that fails -- F0/F1/F2 ARE such probes and are printed rather than promoted to the verdict. MECHANISM, from the spec's own algebra: u = P_IB g + P_II u exactly, so gbar is literally the first Neumann term of the label's defining recursion and a linear probe handed it performs one hop of the iteration the architecture is supposed to perform; that one column moves the median from 1.0192 to 0.7639. Bounded on the other side too: 0/28 reach PASS_BAR 0.5, so the probe does not READ the label -- the remaining P_II u is a global solve at lambda_2 ~ 0.95. THE VERDICT TURNS ON A DECLARATION THE CORPUS DOES NOT MAKE: admissible 28/28 on F0-F2, inadmissible 25/28 on F3, and nothing in the corpus says whether g is readable one hop away in whatever x a consumer builds. Amendment: the corpus must declare its tensorisation before C-B has an answer. verdict: COUNTS -- five categories, and the fifth is carried forward

verdict: COORDINATOR DEFECT CONFIRMED AND FIXED -- one guard, robustness not vacuity
text: The coordinator's static-analysis lead on scale/r10_admissibility.py was checked against the block structure and is REAL, unlike the three false positives forwarded earlier this round. binding_crossover(host.available_mib, card.free_mib) sat inside the demo()'s 'if card is not None' branch but outside any host guard, and vram_gate.read_host() returns None when psutil is absent (scale/vram_gate.py:122-125), so a box with nvidia-smi and no psutil would raise AttributeError. Severity as scoped: it CRASHES rather than passing silently, so it is a robustness gap and cannot produce a false GREEN; and it is UNREACHABLE on this box because psutil is installed, which is precisely why a run would never have found it. Fixed with one guard -- 'if card is not None and host is not None' -- and a comment naming the branch, since a module that prices memory should be the one module that survives being unable to read memory. Nothing else restructured. main() already carried the both-resources guard.

C-C IS A GREEN NOBODY EARNED, AND ITS FORMULA UNDER-PRICES BY 64x. The clause 4*n*s*d*heads reads 512.0 MiB against 8,585,740,288 card bytes and passes. Two things are wrong with that pass. (1) THE FORMULA IS THE WRONG TENSOR: the peak is the [n, s, s] operator, not the projections, so the clause under-prices the shipped harness by exactly s/d = 64. At batch 8192 with s=1024 the clause reads 512 MiB and the real tensor is 32,768 MiB -- FOUR TIMES THE WHOLE CARD. A clause that passes at 512 MiB is certifying a job that cannot fit. (2) VRAM NEVER BINDS ANYWAY: at the round's declared 2 GiB host budget the host refuses at batch 8,832 while VRAM would not refuse until batch 101,837 -- 11.53x later, with the card at 9% of free when the box is already out of memory. This is the same defect the campaign measured at it.8, when require(4275, name='capacity-sweep') returned FITS citing 7162 MiB of free VRAM for a CPU-only job: a clause satisfied against the wrong resource.

C-A FAILS AND WAS ILL-POSED. The corpus declares NO train/eval split at all, so the clause cannot be evaluated until one is declared -- both partitions a reader could take were measured rather than one being chosen quietly. On the split that fails: 12 SHARED GRAPHS with BIT-IDENTICAL labels, accounting for 43.66% of eval rows. That is the exact shape the clause exists for: the script names the `impact` task dying at linear-probe train 4.93e-08 against eval 1.478, an eight-order gap that means memorisation rather than learning.

C-B FAILS 25 OF 28 RUNGS PLUS BOTH POOLED SPLITS, AND THE VERDICT TURNS ON A MISSING DECLARATION. Median within-split linear-probe NRMSE is 0.7639 against a bar of 0.9 -- a LINEAR PROBE BEATS THE BAR, so on those features the task is not measuring what the architecture claims. But the corpus declares no feature set either: on strictly GEOMETRIC features it is admissible 28 of 28; adding ONE local read of the boundary data makes it inadmissible 25 of 28. So the corpus is admissible or inadmissible depending on a choice nobody has written down, and the honest report is that the declaration is missing rather than picking the features that give the preferred verdict.
