SATURN also caught that the RSS fit residual is 10.1 MiB where it.8 said 'within 10' -- corrected in the same docstring, because a fit residual rounded in the flattering direction is the same defect at a smaller scale.

THE C-C VRAM CLAUSE HAS NO REACHABLE FAILURE STATE, and SATURN asserted that rather than reporting a pass. All 25 VRAM rows are INAPPLICABLE and 0 passed. At the round's declared 2 GiB host budget the host refuses at batch 8,832 with the card at 690 MiB = 9% of free; VRAM does not refuse until batch 101,837, which is 11.53x later and beyond any shape this corpus reaches. So the clause cannot fire, at any shape, ever -- and 101,837 > 8,832 is itself asserted in the code so the vacuity is executable rather than argued. A clause with no reachable failure state that reports GREEN is the exact shape this campaign catalogues, and here it is inside the admissibility battery that admits the corpus.

THE C-A FAILURE HAS A CAUSE WORTH RECORDING: the reproduction that earned trust in one dimension destroyed it in another. Arm 'reproduce' IS it.14's corpus by design -- that bit-for-bit reproduction (lambda_2 delta 0.0) is what made it.15's second oracle trustworthy. It is also exactly what makes the two FILES an unusable train/eval split: 12 shared graphs, labelled-identical, 43.66% of eval rows. And the failure direction is the OPPOSITE end from the `impact` case the clause was written for: impact died at train 4.93e-08 vs eval 1.478 with NOTHING leaked and cos(w0,w1) = -1.077e-08 making transfer impossible; this leaks everything and fails optimistic. Same disease, opposite ends. C-B's mechanism is equally exact: u = P_IB g + P_II u, so `gbar` is literally the first Neumann term of the label's own recursion -- the probe is not finding a shortcut, it is reading the recursion.

THREE FOR THREE: EVERY PRE-REGISTERED RULE CHECKED AGAINST ITS OWN DESIGN SURVIVES AS A DECISION PROCEDURE AND FAILS AS A JUSTIFICATION. it.11's threshold (N=8 seed CI excluding 1.0) is met and correct, while the interval a reader would naturally check -- the boot_lo/boot_hi every cell ships -- resamples eval examples inside one model and answers a different question. it.12's threshold (k >= 18 of 20) is met at 19, while the p it quotes, C(20,<=2)*0.5^20 = 2.012e-4, is a SIGN-TEST p-value: nothing makes 0.5 the null crossing rate for a continuous NRMSE against a fixed bar, and the 20 draws share one graph, one partition and one split. it.16 C-C passes 25/25 shapes while its formula 4*n*s*d*heads prices the PROJECTIONS when the shipped peak is the [n,s,s] operator -- under by exactly s/d = 64, reading 512 MiB where the tensor is 32,768 MiB. THE ASYMMETRY IS THE POINT: a wrong THRESHOLD is caught the first time someone disputes a verdict; a wrong JUSTIFICATION beside a correct threshold is never caught, because the verdicts keep coming out right -- and the justification is the part a reader reuses. k>=18 needs no null at all; the null was decoration that looked like rigour. Filed SEPARATELY from the 22-instance catalogue because it is a different mechanism and the instance count must not be inflated by it.

VERIFIED BEFORE RELAYING, which this round's author has failed to do five times. SATURN's C-C claim that 4*n*s*d*heads under-prices by exactly s/d = 64 holds on inspection: m3_capability.py:143 produces the projections q, k at [n, s, d_model]; :144 is `a = self._operator(q, k)` carrying the shape annotation `# [n,s,s]` IN THE SOURCE; and :108-109 build ONE wq and ONE wk, so heads=1 is the construction rather than a convention. The clause prices q or k; the peak is a. Ratio s/d_model = 1024/16 = 64, as reported. The consequence stands: at batch 8192, s=1024, the clause reads 512 MiB and the real tensor is 32,768 MiB, four times the 8188 MiB card, so a clause that passes is certifying a job that cannot fit.

PHASE 1B'S EXIT GATE WILL FAIL AS THINGS STAND, AND THE REPAIR IS TWO DECLARATIONS, NOT TWO FIXES. it.19 requires C-A..C-F ALL GREEN for registration; C-A and C-B already fail, so the registration verdict is NOT REGISTERED unless the corpus is amended. Both failures are ill-posedness rather than defect, and SATURN measured both branches instead of picking one. (1) SPLIT: the corpus declares no train/eval split. Split by FILE (it14|it15) gives 12 shared graphs and 43.66% leaked eval rows; split by ARM (reproduce|widen) gives ZERO shared graphs and 0/5693 leaked. So declaring the split by arm turns C-A green with no change to any instance -- the corpus is admissible under one reading and not the other, and nobody has written down which reading is meant. (2) TENSORISATION: the corpus declares no feature set. On strictly geometric features F0-F2 it is admissible 28/28; adding gbar makes it inadmissible 25/28 with median probe NRMSE 0.7639 against the 0.9 bar. THIS ONE IS NOT A FREE CHOICE: gbar is literally the first Neumann term of u = P_IB g + P_II u, so a model that sees gbar is reading the label's own recursion, and a linear probe beating the bar there means the task cannot measure what the architecture claims. The question 'does the CEQ arm see boundary values?' is therefore an ARCHITECTURAL decision that determines whether the corpus is a test at all, and it belongs to whoever owns the contract. HOUSE is not making either declaration; both are recorded here so it.19 adjudicates against stated options rather than discovering the gap at the gate.

VERIFIED FROM THE SHIPPED ROWS, not the summary, because this claim was relayed to the author as the repair path. results/r10_it16_admissibility.jsonl carries SPLIT-ARM reproduce|widen at shared_graphs=0 over 5693 eval rows with same_graph_family=true, SPLIT-FILE it14|it15 at shared_graphs=12 over 10105, and a plant-leak must-fire row at shared_graphs=1 -- so the clause demonstrably detects a leak rather than passing by blindness. Declaring the split by ARM turns C-A green with no change to any instance, as reported.

WORKING ASSUMPTION DECLARED SO THE LOOP DOES NOT STALL AT it.19, AND FLAGGED FOR THE AUTHOR'S RETURN. Phase 1b's exit gate needs C-A..C-F all green; C-A and C-B fail on ill-posedness and cannot be evaluated until the corpus declares a train/eval split and a tensorisation. Blocking would halt Phase 1c (it.20-24, S1/S2) entirely, so HOUSE proceeds under two stated assumptions rather than stopping. ASSUMPTION 1, SPLIT BY ARM (reproduce|widen): measured at 0 shared graphs over 5693 eval rows against 12 shared and 43.66% leaked for the by-file reading, with a planted-leak must-fire confirming the clause can fire. This is low-risk -- it is the only split of the two that is a split at all. ASSUMPTION 2, GEOMETRIC FEATURES F0-F2, NOT F3: this one is NOT low-risk and is an architectural decision the author owns. The reasoning for assuming it: gbar is the first Neumann term of u = P_IB g + P_II u, so an arm that sees boundary values reads the label's own recursion, a linear probe beats the bar at median 0.7639 against 0.9, and the corpus then measures nothing about architecture. The ONLY reading under which this corpus is a valid test is therefore F0-F2. IF THE AUTHOR INTENDS THE ARM TO SEE BOUNDARY VALUES, this corpus must be rebuilt rather than re-declared, and every downstream S1/S2 result computed under the assumption is void. Recorded before any downstream work so the dependency is visible rather than discovered later.

THE MONOTONICITY ASSUMPTION'S FIRST VIOLATION APPEARS AT THE FIRST RUNG BEYOND THE FITTED RANGE -- instance 22's lesson in a second quantity. JUPITER's it.10 isotonic fit reported max violation EXACTLY 0.0 across all nine sequences, which was true and was true only within the span he had (n = 2048, 8192, 32768). Measured now across t*=32, steps=150, per seed: 12 adjacent pairs, 1 violation, and it is at 32768->49152 on seed 2 (0.997284 -> 0.998811, worsening by +0.001526). Every pair INSIDE the fitted range is monotone; the one counterexample is on the first extrapolated segment. STATED HONESTLY AND NOT OVERCLAIMED: +0.001526 is BELOW the measured cross-thread noise floor of 2.345e-3, so this is a real data point and not a resolvable effect. The correct claim is NOT 'the assumption fails out of range' but 'the first out-of-range evidence is a within-noise violation, where twelve in-range pairs produced none'. It matters because the isotonic fit was the IDENTITY MAP -- it changed nothing precisely because the data was already monotone -- so if that stops holding beyond the grid, the fit starts doing work and its output stops being the raw points.

MARS'S it.4 ATTACK 3 IS STILL LIVE, UNREPAIRED, AND IT SITS IN THE GATE THAT CERTIFIED EVERY BLOCK THIS ROUND. Verified both halves in source. THE CONTROL IS IN-SAMPLE: negation_scope.py trains the two-feature positive control on `feats` (loss = ((net(feats) - target)**2).mean(), :1529) and then scores it on THE SAME feats (out['trained_two_feature'] = nrmse(net(feats)*sigma + mu, y), :1536). THE ARMS ARE HELD-OUT: m3_capability.run_arm scores eval_nrmse = nrmse(pred_eval, y_eval) at :206 against a batch drawn at seed + 12345 (:281, :308). So the clause `trained_two_feature < 1.0` (:1594) that certifies a task as learnable is satisfied by an IN-SAMPLE reading, while every arm it gates must clear 1.0 OUT-OF-SAMPLE. The control is solving an easier problem than the thing it certifies. THE REPO STATES THE RULE THIS VIOLATES, in its own words, in another gate: rips_gate.py:163-168 -- 'A held-out split is not decoration... an in-sample reading would credit memorisation as decoding and the strike below would be unearned.' Two gates ship in one tree and only one obeys it. MEASURED THIS ROUND: trained_two_feature = 0.013981593578261986 at t*=2, in-sample, and BAR CALIBRATED printed in all three blocks. WHAT IT DOES AND DOES NOT COST: it cannot make a crossing false -- t*=2 and t*=8 cross held-out on 8 seeds each and that is independent of how the bar was certified. What it can do is certify a task as learnable when no arm can learn it held-out, which is exactly the reading at t*=32: the bar said learnable, softmax read 1.0034 over 8 seeds. That block's NOT LEARNABLE verdict is therefore consistent with EITHER 'softmax is the limitation' or 'the bar overstated the task', and the round cannot currently tell those apart. Repair is one line -- score the control on a held-out draw, as rips_gate already does -- and it would re-certify every block.

name: tests/loop/test_the_bar_control_is_scored_out_of_sample.py::test_the_bar_control_is_not_scored_on_the_tensor_it_trained_on
text: RED, binding MARS's it.4 attack 3, which had been prose since iteration 4. The guard reads calibrate_bar by AST -- so a rename cannot silently pass -- and reports it exactly: trains the positive control on ['feats'], scores it on ['feats']. THREE COMPANION TESTS PASS AND EACH DOES WORK: (1) the reader finds BOTH call sites, so an empty set cannot make the comparison vacuous; (2) the reader can TELL THE TWO APART -- given a synthetic held-out body it returns {feats} trained and {feats_eval} scored, so a verdict of 'they match' carries information; (3) rips_gate.py STILL HOLDS OUT. That third one exists because this finding's whole argument rests on an in-repo precedent for the correct behaviour, and this round struck its author FIVE TIMES for accepting citations that arrived inside good work. A load-bearing citation now gets an executable check instead of a line number: if rips_gate stops holding out, this file fails and says the precedent moved, rather than quoting it forever.

THE VERIFY-BEFORE-FORWARDING RULE PAID OFF, MEASURABLY. A static analyzer reported `_rel` undefined at r10_it17_battery.py:424 and :437. Checked first: _rel is defined at :375, so the hit was a snapshot of a file being actively written, not a claim about the code. NOT forwarded. Running record on static-analysis leads this round: three forwarded WITHOUT checking (r10_corpus_spec import symbol, two arity hits, JUPITER's redeclared isofit) and all three were false positives that each cost an agent a verification pass; two checked before sending, of which one was real (host.available_mib unguarded inside the card branch, confirmed and fixed by SATURN) and one was this false positive, caught. The rule: on a file under active write, an analyzer's complaint is a snapshot of a moment rather than a statement about the source, and the cost of checking is seconds against a recipient's minutes.

THE IN-SAMPLE CONTROL IS ISOLATED, NOT SYSTEMIC -- swept rather than assumed, because finding one instance is a reason to look for more (instance 23's lesson: a repair at one site is not a repaired repo). Method: walk scale/*.py by AST, keep every FunctionDef containing a .step() call, and within each compare the tensors passed to net(...) on training lines (loss/backward) against those on scoring lines (nrmse/score). RESULT: 1 function examined, 1 in-sample -- negation_scope.py::calibrate_bar, trains ['feats'], scores ['feats']. No other gate in scale/ has the pattern. SCOPE STATED BECAUSE THE DENOMINATOR IS SMALL: the sweep matches only the net(...) idiom and only functions with a .step() call, so m3_capability.run_arm does not appear -- it trains and scores through raw_pred. That one was verified separately and is HELD-OUT (eval_nrmse = nrmse(pred_eval, y_eval) at :206, batch drawn at seed + 12345 at :281 and :308). '1 examined' is an honest count of what the sweep could see, not a claim that only one function in the repo trains and scores.

SELF-STRIKE, AN AGGREGATE READ AS ITS ELEMENTS, COMMITTED WHILE REPORTING ON THAT EXACT DEFECT. HOUSE stated '4 of 8 seeds at n=49152, mean 0.998674, all below the bar' from the MEAN without checking the individual values. Seed 3 reads 1.000584, ABOVE the bar. The correct count is 3 below, 1 above. A mean under a threshold does not imply every element is under it, and the sentence asserted the second from the first.

REGRESSION TOWARD THE MEAN AT THE NEW RUNG, AND IT IS THE LUCKY SEEDS THAT GIVE GROUND. t*=32, steps=150, per seed across n=32768 -> n=49152: seed 0 1.006066 -> 0.999940 (-0.006126), seed 1 1.003982 -> 0.995362 (-0.008620), seed 2 0.997284 -> 0.998811 (+0.001526), seed 3 0.998440 -> 1.000584 (+0.002144). THE TWO THAT WORSENED ARE EXACTLY THE TWO THAT HAD CROSSED AT n=32768 -- seeds 2 and 3 were the only pair below the bar at that rung and both drifted back up, while the two that were above improved by 3-4x larger deltas. Both upward deltas sit at or below the 2.345e-3 noise floor and are not resolvable worsenings; both downward deltas are well above it. This is the shape that makes a single-draw reading at a marginal cell untrustworthy in BOTH directions, and it is why the it.11 gate refuses until N=8: at n=32768 a single draw reported LEARNS 25% of the time, and at n=49152 the seeds that produced those readings are the ones now reporting the opposite.

ADDENDUM TO THE AGGREGATE STRIKE: THE INSTRUMENT WAS RIGHT THERE AND WAS BYPASSED. The n=49152 monitor was built by HOUSE to print the under-bar COUNT explicitly -- its event line reads 'N/8 cells | best X | K under the bar' -- precisely so a mean could not be mistaken for a tally. At the 4/8 point it reported '3 under the bar', which is correct. HOUSE did not wait for it, computed the mean independently, and asserted 'all below the bar' from that. So the failure was not a missing instrument or an instrument that lied; it was an available correct reading, discarded in favour of a quicker derivation that answered a different question. That is the same shape as instance 23 (a correct instrument, a reader taking more from it than it said) with an extra turn: here the reader did not even consult the instrument he had built for this exact purpose.

THE BAR IS DEFINITIONAL, SO THE CROSSINGS ARE UNTOUCHED -- verified rather than assumed. nrmse (negation_scope.py:1382-1387) is RMSE divided by std(y), so the mean predictor reads exactly 1.0 BY CONSTRUCTION. NRMSE < 1.0 is therefore not a calibrated threshold and cannot be moved by how the positive control was scored. t*=2 [0.9462,0.9591] and t*=8 [0.9739,0.9768] read below a DEFINITIONAL bar on HELD-OUT data over 8 seeds each, and the in-sample-control finding does not reach them. WHAT IT DOES REACH, EXACTLY: the certification that a task is worth testing at all. If the control were scored held-out and read >= 1.0, calibrate_bar prints BAR BROKEN and NO ARM IS SCORED. So the t*=32 caveat has a precise form: that block may be a task no model can learn held-out, in which case softmax's 1.0034 says nothing about softmax.

THE IN-SAMPLE CONTROL SURVIVED A REPAIR PASS THAT REMOVED TWO SIBLINGS FROM THE SAME FUNCTION. calibrate_bar's own docstring (negation_scope.py:1414-1425) records that two of its three original clauses were ALGEBRAIC IDENTITIES rather than measurements: predict_the_mean = nrmse(y.mean(), y) == 1.0 by definition of nrmse, and oracle = nrmse(oracle(x,f,p), y) == 0.0 because make_batch RETURNS oracle(x,f,p) as y -- so nrmse(t,t) was being compared to zero. The docstring names the class: 'this project's zero BY CONSTRUCTION mapped to GREEN defect, sitting in the gate that decides whether any arm is credited.' Both were found and repaired. THE THIRD INSTANCE, IN THE SAME FUNCTION, WAS LEFT: a positive control trained and scored on identical feats, certifying learnability from an in-sample reading. A sweep that removes two members of a class from one function and leaves a third is the strongest available argument for counting what was EXAMINED rather than what was FOUND -- and this round's own sweep for the same pattern across scale/ found exactly one function, which is that one.

EXACTLY ONE OF bar_verdict's FIVE CLAUSES TESTS LEARNABILITY, AND IT IS THE IN-SAMPLE ONE. Read in full at negation_scope.py:1580-1598. (1) abs(predict_the_mean - 1.0) > 1e-6 -- an IDENTITY (1.0 by definition of nrmse), honestly repurposed as an nrmse implementation self-check, message 'nrmse is mis-implemented'. (2) payload_only >= 1.0 -- a real measurement, reads 1.2272, checks the label is not the payload. (3) oracle < 1e-6 -- also an IDENTITY (make_batch RETURNS oracle(x,f,p) as y), repurposed as an oracle-wiring self-check. (4) flipper_dependence within tol of the closed form -- a real measurement, 1.4012436552 against 2/sqrt(2)=1.4142135624 at tol 0.05, checks this is the INTENDED task. (5) trained_two_feature < 1.0 -- the only clause that asks whether ANYTHING can learn this task, and its control is trained and scored on identical feats. CONSEQUENCE: two clauses check the implementation, two check the corpus is the intended corpus, and the entire learnability certification rests on ONE clause scored in-sample. There is no second opinion in this gate and the other four cannot substitute -- they answer different questions. NOTE IN THE GATE'S FAVOUR: both identities are named as identities in the docstring and were DELIBERATELY repurposed into implementation self-checks rather than left looking like task measurements. That is the correct treatment of a by-construction clause, and it is exactly what makes the third one's survival conspicuous.

THE IN-SAMPLE CONTROL COSTS THIS ROUND NOTHING -- MEASURED, NOT ARGUED, AND THE REPLICATION IS BOUND TO THE SHIPPED READING FIRST. Replicated calibrate_bar's positive control faithfully (same net Linear(k,32)/GELU/Linear(32,1), same normal_(0,0.5) init under Generator().manual_seed(seed), zeroed biases, same Adam lr, same target standardisation and un-standardisation) and PINNED to the sweep's own call at r10_capacity_sweep.py:160 -- n=N_EVAL=4096, s=64, d=24, steps=600. FIRST ATTEMPT USED steps=150 AND n=2048 AND DID NOT REPRODUCE (0.031205 against a shipped 0.013982); a replication that does not reproduce the shipped number proves nothing about a number it derives. Pinned correctly it reproduces to 1.976e-08, five orders inside this repo's own measured cross-thread drift of 2.345e-03. HELD-OUT READINGS, scored on a batch drawn at seed+12345 and never trained on: t*=2 0.018030 (in-sample 0.013982, gap +0.004048), t*=8 0.032861 (0.022470, +0.010391), t*=32 0.026544 (0.024554, +0.001990). ALL THREE PASS the clause's 1.0 threshold by a factor of ~38 at the worst block. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ROUND: the defect is real -- the clause is in-sample, it is the ONLY one of bar_verdict's five that tests learnability, and it survived a repair pass that removed two by-construction siblings from the same function -- and its cost here is ZERO, because the certification passes either way. THIS RESOLVES THE t*=32 INTERPRETATION: the task IS learnable held-out by a two-feature control at 0.026544, so softmax reading 1.0034 there is a statement about SOFTMAX, not about an uncertifiable task. The NOT LEARNABLE verdict means what it appeared to mean. Probe kept at scale/heldout_control_probe.py so the measurement is re-runnable rather than quoted.

C-F(a) FAILS 12 OF 12: THE do()-BIT DOES NOT MOVE THE LABEL BY THE FILED delta. delta = 0.5 was filed BEFORE measurement; measured fd_min ranges 0.000000 to 0.359833 and only 1 of 324 do()-bits clears it. WORSE, ONE BIT MOVES THE LABEL BY EXACTLY 0.0 IN EVERY NORM: reproduce-n1024-d4-t0.95, seed 0x3a14000a, ships a boundary node ALL OF WHOSE NEIGHBOURS ARE ALSO BOUNDARY NODES. Not a plant -- nothing in spec.stratify forbids one. A causal intervention with no causal effect, emitted by the corpus builder itself, in a corpus whose whole purpose is causal consequence.

C-F(b): THE INSTRUMENT WORKS AND THIS ROUND'S OWN CONTROLS DO NOT USE IT. MARS's front-door classifier agrees with scale/p1prime.py on 191/191 files, so the instrument is bound to the repo's existing measurement of the same property. The finding is what it then measures: THE 12 CONTROLS THIS ROUND HAS BEEN USING ENTER BELOW make_rung, LEAVING 5 STAGES UNEXERCISED. And the demonstration that makes L-SCOPE concrete rather than doctrinal: a HAND-BUILT star graph reads fd = 2.000000 where every front-door instance reads under 0.36, and NO PRODUCTION BUILDER CAN EMIT THAT STAR. So a hand-built control turns C-F from failed into ok -- the clause passes on an input the production path cannot produce. That is exactly the P1 -> P1' lesson this campaign withdrew a presumption over, shown in the corpus's own units instead of argued.

C-D HOLDS 12/12 AND ITS WITNESS IS IN TENSION WITH C-B. khop_128 -- 128 rounds of the message passing the architecture is supposed to do, UNTRAINED -- reads 0.005092 on reproduce-n128-d4-t0.95 against a mean-predictor control at exactly 1.000000. But the it.16 linear probe ALSO reads under 1.0 on 10 of 12 rungs, and that is the SAME READING THAT FAILS C-B. One measurement satisfies the clause requiring an arm to succeed and fails the clause requiring a probe to fail; the battery's two clauses pull against each other on one number. SECOND RESULT: the k-hop arm does not cross 1.0 until between k=32 and k=64 -- at k=32 it reads 1.4782, WORSE than predicting the mean, because the label has a large mean and a small spread so a truncated arm pays for the mean before it earns any variance. C-E(i) holds 12/12 (sensitivity to g 2.29e-01..6.93e-01, determinism 0.0, second route 1.554e-15). C-E(ii) holds WITH A DENOMINATOR: 0 stored label vectors in 5,461 files and 142,271,756 bytes EXAMINED, plus 56 two-coordinate disclosures in one file reported rather than dropped.

PHASE 1B REGISTRATION VERDICT: NOT REGISTERED. it.19 requires C-A..C-F all GREEN and four fail. C-A: split undeclared, 12 shared graphs and 43.66% leaked eval rows on the by-file reading (0 shared by arm). C-B: linear probe beats the bar on gbar features, median 0.7639 against 0.9. C-C: reports GREEN while pricing the wrong tensor by s/d = 64 against a resource that never binds (VRAM refuses at batch 101,837, host at 8,832). C-F: the do()-bit moves labels by at most 0.359833 against a filed delta of 0.5, 1 of 324 bits clearing it, and one bit moving by exactly 0.0. TWO KINDS OF FAILURE, and they need different repairs: C-A and C-B are ILL-POSEDNESS the corpus can declare its way out of (a split, a tensorisation) with no instance changed; C-C and C-F are DEFECTS needing repair (the formula prices projections not the operator; stratify can emit a boundary node whose neighbours are all boundary nodes, so a do() has nowhere to propagate). THE MOST EXPENSIVE FINDING IS NOT IN THE VERDICT: C-F(b) measured that the 12 controls THIS ROUND has been using enter BELOW make_rung, leaving 5 stages unexercised, and demonstrated the cost -- a hand-built star graph reads fd=2.000000 where every front-door instance reads under 0.36, and no production builder can emit that star. So a hand-built control PASSES the clause real inputs FAIL. That applies retroactively to control-based claims already published in this round's records, and is recorded rather than buried.

C-D HOLDS 12/12. Arm khop_128 (u_k = sum_{m<k} P_II^m P_IB g, untrained, reads only adj/B/g), cell reproduce-n128-d4-t0.95 (n=128, mean_deg=4, seed 0x3a140002, lambda_2=0.9455579636, |B|=11, |I|=117), NRMSE=0.005092 against a predict-the-mean control at exactly 1.000000. The bar is not a pick: rips_gate.nrmse normalises by sd(y) so the mean predictor is 1.0 by construction (scale/rips_gate.py:118-127). THE CROSSING IS LATE AND UNIFORM: khop_32's corpus-wide MINIMUM is 1.098575 and khop_64's corpus-wide MAXIMUM is 0.612136, so thirty-two rounds of message passing is worse than the mean on every one of the twelve rungs. TENSION RECORDED: probe_F3 also reads under 1.0 on 10/12 (min 0.566979, median 0.745818), and that is cell-for-cell the same reading it.16 sec 3.3 publishes as C-B's FAILURE against FAIL_BAR=0.9. A corpus whose only C-D witness is its C-B violation has shown nothing but that the trivial probe succeeds, which is why the verdict is taken on khop_128. it.16 published its failure tables BEFORE C-D was established; they are admissible in retrospect and the order is recorded rather than tidied. MUST-FIRE bound to a CONSTRUCTED label (permutation, seed 0x3a170001, declared in the module header before the run): best arm 0.005531 -> 1.421956, which is sqrt(2) to three figures and exactly what E||y - perm y||^2 = 2 n var(y) predicts; the verdict flips to failed.

C-E HOLDS ON BOTH PROPERTIES, AND THE SCAN IS NOT EMPTY. (i) EXECUTABLE, 12/12: spec.resolvent_oracle (scale/r10_corpus_spec.py:254) takes (P_II, P_IB, g) and nothing else, so no path exists by which a stored label reaches it; measured sensitivity to g 2.286245e-01..6.934776e-01, determinism deviation 0.0 bitwise on 12/12, second route (dual.kirchhoff_extension, 324 cofactor solves) 2.776e-16..1.554e-15 against the imported kirchhoff.AGREEMENT_TOL=1e-10. End-to-end executability: all 28 shipped it.15 rungs regenerated from four scalars with recovery_max_range_delta = 0.0. MUST-FIRE: an oracle that ignores its arguments and returns the cached label is numerically perfect and is refused by the sensitivity property alone, sensitivity 0.0 <= 1e-10. (ii) ZERO ANSWER KEYS, WITH THE DENOMINATOR: 46,557 files walked; 35,950 excluded by declaration (lean/.lake, the vendored Lake build cache) and 3,055 (.git); 2,089 skipped as non-UTF-8 and 2 as over 16 MiB; 5,461 EXAMINED, 142,271,756 bytes read, 280 search literals over all 28 label vectors. STRUCTURAL route (any JSON list of >=16 numbers matching a label vector inside 1e-10): 0 hits. TEXTUAL route: 56 hits, every one of them in results/r10_it15_dual_oracle.jsonl and every one the u_absorbing_range field, 28 rungs x 2 floats. Coordinates 0, middle and last were searched with the same needles and appear nowhere, which is what makes the 56 a measurement of a known field rather than an accident. Verdict holds on the clause as written; the recorded surface is 2 of |I| label coordinates per rung, 3.5 percent of the label at n=64 and 0.21 percent at n=1024. Smallest amendment if literal zero disclosure is wanted: ship a hash of u instead of its extremes. n=49152 IS SITTING ON THE CROSSING POINT, AND JUPITER PREDICTED WHERE. At 5 of 8 seeds the t*=32 readings are 0.995362, 0.998811, 0.999940, 1.000205, 1.000584 -- THREE OF FIVE WITHIN 0.0006 OF THE BAR. That is the shape of a crossing POINT: a distribution centred on 1.0, not a clean flip. JUPITER's it.10 frontier fit put the crossing at n* = 48,823 by linear interpolation in log2(n) from three rungs; this cell is n=49152, 0.7% above it, and the seeds straddle the bar. A prediction extrapolated 0.58 octaves beyond the measured grid landed on a distribution centred at the threshold. THE PER-SEED DIRECTION ALSO HOLDS: every seed that was ABOVE the bar at n=32768 improved (0: -0.006126, 1: -0.008620, 4: -0.003108) and both that were BELOW drifted up (2: +0.001526, 3: +0.002144), with the improvements 2-4x larger than the regressions. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE VERDICT: with the mass this close to 1.0 the N=8 seed CI could plausibly land either side, which is exactly why it.11's gate refuses until all eight exist. A verdict published at 5 seeds here would be a coin flip dressed as a measurement, and the round has already measured that failure mode one rung down, where 2 of 8 seeds crossed and a single draw reported the opposite 25% of the time.

PARTIAL STRIKE ON C-F: THE 12/12 FAILURE IS A THRESHOLD-IMPORT ERROR, NOT A CORPUS DEFECT. Measured from MARS's own shipped rows: fd_max x |B| is NEAR-CONSTANT at 3.741 across all twelve rungs (range 2.341-5.220), which is harmonic measure -- one boundary node's influence on the interior is ~1/|B|. So fd >= 0.5 requires |B| <= 7.5, and the stratified corpus runs |B| = 4..80. TEN OF TWELVE RUNGS CANNOT REACH THE THRESHOLD BY CONSTRUCTION, because stratify targets lambda_2 in [0.90,0.95] and that forces large boundaries. PROVENANCE OF THE NUMBER, from MARS's own delta_source field: delta=0.5 was imported from scale/negation_scope.py:1587, the CHAIN task's flipper_dependence > 0.5 clause. That threshold was written for a construction whose closed form is 2/sqrt(t*) -- which itself drops below 0.5 at t* > 16, so the chain clause would fail on the CHAIN at t*=32 where the value is 0.3536. MARS did the right thing (import a threshold rather than re-pick one that flatters the result) and got a wrong number, because that rule has an unstated precondition: THE SOURCE MUST MEASURE THE SAME PHYSICAL QUANTITY. Importing across task families transports a number without its units. WHAT SURVIVES THE STRIKE: the zero-bit. reproduce-n1024-d4-t0.95 has a boundary node with NO INTERIOR NEIGHBOUR, so a do() has nowhere to propagate -- fd exactly 0.0 in every norm. That is a real generation gap, independent of any threshold, and nothing in spec.stratify forbids it.

THE IMPORT-DON'T-RE-PICK RULE HAS AN UNSTATED PRECONDITION, AND THIS ROUND JUST PAID FOR IT. Four separate briefs this round instructed agents to IMPORT thresholds that already exist rather than choose ones that flatter the result, and agents complied well: SATURN imported kirchhoff.AGREEMENT_TOL by OBJECT IDENTITY so a local re-pick fails the self-check, and imported rips_gate.FAIL_BAR = 0.9 for C-B. Both were correct because both measured the same quantity as their source. MARS imported delta=0.5 from the chain task's flipper clause and applied it to a harmonic corpus whose causal effect scales as 1/|B|. The rule as stated -- 'import thresholds that exist rather than re-picking one that flatters your result' -- does not say the source must measure the SAME PHYSICAL QUANTITY, and without that clause it licenses transporting a number across task families where it means something else. The corrected rule: import a threshold only from a source measuring the same quantity in the same units, and state which quantity that is. An imported number carries the authority of having been used before, which is precisely the credibility-transfer defect this catalogue records at instance 19 -- applied to constants instead of claims.

SATURN'S THRESHOLD IMPORT VERIFIED CORRECT, in contrast to MARS's. rips_gate.py:61 defines FAIL_BAR = 0.9 with the comment 'the decoder is doing essentially nothing', in NRMSE units, and impact.py:1121 uses it in exactly that role -- 'planted single-asset local probe must FAIL', checking score_local_r0 >= 0.9. C-B's role is identical: a within-split linear probe must read ABOVE the bar. Same quantity, same role, same units. The import is sound and the object-identity assertion in demo() means a local re-pick fails the self-check.

THE ACTIONABLE FORM OF THE IMPORT RULE: A THRESHOLD TRAVELS IFF ITS QUANTITY HAS A CONSTRUCTION-INDEPENDENT ANCHOR. Two imports this round, both principled, one sound and one not, and the difference is not 'same physical quantity' but whether the units are anchored. NRMSE IS ANCHORED: 1.0 is predict-the-mean BY CONSTRUCTION for any task at any scale, because nrmse is RMSE divided by std(y) (negation_scope.py:1382-1387). So FAIL_BAR = 0.9 in NRMSE means the same thing in every task family, and SATURN's C-B import is sound. FLIPPER_DEPENDENCE IS NOT ANCHORED: it is |label move| / |label scale|, and its achievable range is set by the generator -- 2/sqrt(t*) for the chain, ~3.741/|B| for the harmonic corpus (measured: fd_max x |B| near-constant at 3.741 over twelve rungs). A threshold in those units is meaningless without the construction that produced it, so MARS's delta=0.5 import transported a number out of its units. RULE, stated so it can be applied: before importing a threshold, ask what value the quantity takes under a null or trivial predictor. If that value is a construction-independent constant, the threshold travels. If it depends on the generator's parameters, it does not.

SCOPING MARS'S C-F(b) FINDING RETROACTIVELY, so it is not read wider than it measures. His result is that the 12 CONTROLS the round has been using enter BELOW make_rung with 5 stages unexercised. Read carelessly that invalidates every planted control this round. CHECKED, and it does not reach it.15's. scale/r10_dual_oracle.py:232 takes adj, boundary, g straight from inst -- the instance arrives FROM THE CORPUS GENERATOR, front door -- and the plant is applied at :240 as defect=plant is not None INSIDE absorbing_extension, corrupting the ORACLE UNDER TEST rather than the input. That is the correct construction for testing an oracle: production input, defect injected into the instrument. So the it.15 rejection rates STAND: 29/29 absorbing-side, 17/17 Kirchhoff-side, and the 0/17 SHARED-plant blind spot, which is built the same way and is the finding that matters most there. WHAT MARS'S RESULT DOES REACH is the C-F controls specifically, where the input itself is constructed -- and his star graph shows the cost concretely: fd = 2.000000 on an input no production builder can emit, against under 0.36 for every front-door instance. A finding about where CONTROL INPUTS enter is not a finding about where PLANTS are injected, and the two were worth separating before the wider reading propagated into the round record.

THE REGRESSION PATTERN IS NOW 6 FOR 6 AND ASYMMETRIC. t*=32, n=32768 -> n=49152, per seed: every seed that was ABOVE the bar improved (0: -0.006126, 1: -0.008620, 4: -0.003108, 5: -0.009272) and every seed that was BELOW worsened (2: +0.001526, 3: +0.002144). Four for four and two for two. THE MAGNITUDES ARE ASYMMETRIC BY ~4x: improvements average -0.0068, regressions average +0.0018. Seed 5 was the WORST cell at n=32768 (1.008121) and is now under the bar at 0.998849, the largest single move measured. MECHANISM: seeds far above the bar have room to improve with more data; seeds already below were there partly on luck, and more data pulls them toward the true mean. Opposite signs, different magnitudes -- the signature of regression toward a mean sitting near the threshold. CONSEQUENCE: the running mean is 0.998959 with 4 of 6 under, and the mass is within a thousandth of 1.0, so the N=8 verdict is still not safe to call. This is the concrete case for it.11's refusal: at n=32768 a single draw reported the opposite verdict 25% of the time, and at n=49152 the seeds that produced those readings are the two now reporting the other way.

name: tests/loop/test_every_boundary_node_can_propagate.py::test_no_corpus_instance_has_a_boundary_node_that_cannot_propagate
text: RED, binding the ONE part of C-F that survives its threshold being struck. 1 failed, 14 passed. THE DEFECT: r10_corpus_spec.admissible (JUPITER's Amendment A) checks that every INTERIOR vertex can reach B -- which is exactly what makes (I - P_II) invertible, rho(P_II) < 1 iff every interior state escapes -- and nothing checks the MIRROR: that every BOUNDARY vertex has an INTERIOR neighbour. A boundary node seeing only boundary leaves the resolvent perfectly invertible and simply influences nothing. Measured: reproduce-n1024-d4-t0.95, seed 0x3a14000a, |B|=80 -- the corpus's LARGEST boundary, which is where it should be expected -- do()-bit moves the label by exactly 0.0 in every norm. 1 of 12 rungs. WHY IT OUTLIVES THE STRIKE: C-F's delta=0.5 was struck as imported out of its units (unreachable for |B| > 7.5), but fd = 0.0 fails ANY positive threshold, so this finding is threshold-free. THE 14 PASSES DO WORK: 11 corpus instances pass so the RED is one graph not a blanket condemnation; the deliberate plants are separated from the corpus, since plant-dead-bit carries this defect ON PURPOSE and counting it would fire the guard on its own control; and the plant is asserted to read non-zero, so eleven zeros are distinguishable from a counter that never fires. ROUTE: one clause in admissible, the mirror of the one already there -- every b in B has a neighbour outside B -- then regenerate. Left RED rather than fixed because the twelve rungs already measured were measured on the corpus as it stands, and changing the generator underneath published readings is the worse error.

text: C-C's FORMULA CORRECTION IS NOW EXECUTABLE, 5 passed. Confirms SATURN's finding BEHAVIOURALLY rather than by reading source: a spy on the shipped forward pass observes the actual allocations, so [n,s,s] is measured, not quoted from a comment. Ratio operator/projection = s/d_model holds at three shapes; the absolute figures SATURN reported are asserted arithmetically -- clause 512.0 MiB, peak 32,768.0 MiB, ratio exactly 64. DELIBERATELY GREEN: this holds no defect open, it makes a CORRECTED formula executable so the next person sizing a job reads the peak instead of the projection. That is the failure mode instance 22 already cost this round once, from the permissive direction. TWO DETAILS THAT KEEP IT HONEST: it pins D_MODEL == 16 with a message saying the 64x figure must be RE-DERIVED if that changes rather than silently re-scaled; and it asserts op_elems > proj_elems so a shape where the under-pricing does not arise reports itself as proving nothing instead of passing. ITS OWN MUST-FIRE ALSO FIRED ON FIRST RUN: the spy observed nothing because Arm requires an `s` parameter, and the must-fire caught the empty observation rather than letting three vacuous cases pass.

THE SCOPE CENSUS: 31 controls EXAMINED, 19 FIRE, 18 of the firings PROVEN and 1 SAMPLED, and only 2 of the 19 are defects. HOW R AND D WERE MADE FINITE. R(control) is replaced by the inputs the control is ACTUALLY HANDED; all 31 controls are called at fixed arguments so R is finite and exact, with no proxy on that side -- but R as 'inputs it COULD be handed' is larger, and that narrowing is declared. D is replaced by two objects. D_shipped = the 28 instances dual.reproduce_arm() + dual.widen_arm() actually emit through the FRONT DOOR (29 attempts, 1 band miss carrying no instance), membership by adm.labelled_key SHA-256, exact both ways. D_invariant = five NECESSARY conditions read off the production code: I1 n in {64,128,256,512,1024} (r10_corpus_spec.py:506, r10_dual_oracle.py:124-125); I2 edge count = (n-1)+extra_for(n,d) (r10_admissibility.py:168); I3 connected (r10_corpus_spec.py:145-152); I4 g in [0,1) (r10_dual_oracle.py:325); I5 lambda_2 in [0.90,0.95] (r10_corpus_spec.py:361). Necessary, NEVER sufficient: an input violating one is PROVEN out, an input violating none is UNDECIDED and is not promoted to a membership. Undecided falls back to a SAMPLE of SEARCH_DRAWS=200 production graph draws at the control's own n, imported from spec's own naive_yield(200, SEED0+0x1000) at r10_corpus_spec.py:742 and lifted from its AST, seeds 0x3a180000+i declared before the run. Three further domains, each with its own decidable predicate: D_label (y is producible iff (I-P_II)y is in the column space of P_IB at some g in [0,1); a least-squares residual above 1e-10 PROVES no g produces y), D_resource (36 preflight arguments across scale/*.py taken from the AST -- a line-oriented scan would have found ZERO because both it.16 resource plants are wrapped across lines), D_file (path prefix). Counts over the 33 non-summary rows: passed 29, failed 2, errored 0, inapplicable 0, not_reached 1, unscored 1.

THE TWO DEFECTS, BOTH PROVEN AND BOTH CERTIFYING CONTROLS. (1) it14/path_case, scale/r10_corpus_spec.py:478: the path P_9 with B = the two endpoints and g=(1,0). Proven out of D -- violates I1 (n=9 is not one of the five shapes production is called at), I2 (8 edges is not (n-1)+extra_for for any shipped d at n=9, because there is no shipped d at n=9) and I4. THREE of it.14 sec 2's six agreement rows rest on it alone: 'A vs C (Kirchhoff), 4 path cases 2.220446e-16', 'A vs closed form u_x = 1 - x/(L+1) 2.220446e-16', 'lambda_2 vs cos(pi/(L+1)) 2.220446e-16'. Mitigating and stated: the same oracle pair is certified IN domain at A vs B 9.992007e-16 over 12 rungs (it.14) and A vs Kirchhoff 1.554312e-15 over 29 instances (it.15), so the certification is REDUNDANT rather than absent; what has no in-domain counterpart is the CLOSED FORM, and no closed form exists for a stratified attachment-tree-plus-chords graph, so this control cannot be moved into domain, only labelled. (2) it15/probe-ring-B2, scale/r10_dual_oracle.py:390: the 6-ring at |B|=2, whose own comment names its job as 'the control: applicable and expected to pass, so the two refusals above are not a broken route'. Proven out -- violates I1, I2, I4, I5. Its two siblings probe-B1 and probe-split are correctly out of domain AND THE AUTHOR SAID SO in prose before this census existed (probes() docstring: 'the drawn corpus never hits it -- draw_graph is connected by construction and the stratifier never returned |B| < 4'), which the census confirms mechanically for both. The finding is the THIRD probe: the control certifying the route is healthy runs only on the same out-of-domain ring, so a route that worked on 6-rings and failed on the corpus would pass it. Redundant again -- it.15's headline certifies the same route on 29 in-domain instances -- so it is not load-bearing; it is, as written, unable to bear load. NOT OVERSTATED: both trip I4 (g in [0,1)) only because both hand-set g=(1,0) and rng.uniform(0.0,1.0) excludes 1.0; that invariant is true and thin, and the verdicts stand on I1 and I2, which are about the graph.

THE FIRING RULE AS WRITTEN IS NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT, AND IT GETS 17 OF 19 WRONG. A refusal guard is exercised on inputs production cannot emit BECAUSE THAT IS WHAT A REFUSAL GUARD IS FOR. AMENDMENT, stated not applied to anyone else's code: the rule must be conditioned on the control's declared ROLE -- certifying (its reading supports a claim about production; firing is a defect), excluding (it exercises a refusal; firing is expected and the obligation is instead a paired in-domain control that does NOT fire), illustrating (it demonstrates a hazard; firing is the result). Filed BEFORE any control was scored, alongside the firing rule itself. Applied to this registry: 19 firings become 2 defects -- 13 refusal guards doing their job and 4 hazard demonstrations whose entire content is that they are out of domain. THIS PUTS THE CLAUSE IN DIRECT TENSION WITH A STANDING ROUND LAW: 'bind a must-fire to a constructed input, so its reachability cannot depend on live data' forces exactly the shape this clause fires on. Both rules are right; they apply to different roles and neither says so on its own. ROLE IS DECLARED, NOT MEASURED, and that is a limitation rather than a design choice: whether a reading certifies production is a fact about the report that quotes it, not about the input, so a mislabelled role produces a wrong verdict this census will not notice. SECOND, SMALLER AMENDMENT: R should be the set of inputs a control CAN be handed, not the set it IS handed; they coincide for all 31 here because all 31 are called at fixed arguments, but a control taking a caller-supplied seed range would need that range declared first. SANITY CHECK THE CENSUS PASSES: 7 of the 20 excluding controls do NOT fire, and mechanically so -- a plant on the INSTRUMENT (must_fire_oracle, must_fire_dose, check_instance's three, demonstrate_halt, plant-leak) leaves the INPUT in domain, while a plant on the input takes it out; a census returning 'everything fires' would have been worth nothing.

PROVEN AGAINST SAMPLED, WHICH IS THE WHOLE CLAUSE. 18 of 19 firings are PROVEN, by four distinct decision procedures: 11 by a violated necessary invariant (instance domain), 3 by a least-squares residual certifying that NO g produces the label (D_label -- the strongest of the four, since it rules out every g rather than reporting that none was found), 2 by the request not being a literal production issues (D_resource), 2 by a path predicate (D_file). ONE firing is SAMPLED ONLY: it18/plant-relabelled, a real front-door instance with two node labels transposed and the boundary carried along, so same n, same edge count, same connectivity, same g, same lambda_2 -- it violates NO invariant -- and its graph key was not found in 400 production draws at n=64 (200 declared seeds x the two shipped mean degrees at that n). FOR THAT CONTROL THE CENSUS CANNOT DISTINGUISH R n D = empty FROM R n D SMALL AND UNSAMPLED, AND DOES NOT CLAIM TO: a relabelled draw is in the support of spec.draw_graph, which draws a uniform permutation, so the transposed graph has exactly the same probability as the original. The row reads strength=sampled, not proven. That control exists for this purpose -- without it the sampled branch would never have executed, and a branch that never runs is the failure mode this round already catalogued once -- and it is constructed, so its reachability does not depend on the live tree. BOTH DEFECTS ARE PROVEN, NOT SAMPLED, so the two verdicts the census turns on rest on the strong half of the mechanization. MUST-FIRES, all constructed and all asserted in demo(): must-NOT-fire on a front-door instance (in D, proven by labelled-key match); I3 plant (n=64, production edge count, two components) out by I3 AND I5 -- it was written as a single-invariant plant and MEASURED as a two-invariant one, and is reported as one; I4 plant (a real instance with g == 7.5) out by I4 alone, the single-invariant plant on this census; I1 plant (6-node ring) out by I1, I2, I5; the sampled branch; the label domain both ways (real u in, shuffled u out at residual 1.436e-01 against 1e-10); and the role rule both ways, the same firing control scoring ok as excluding and failed as certifying. GATE: preflight(0, name='r10-it18-scope-census', host_mib=512) returned HOST FITS, needs 640 MiB, 2141 MiB available at the census and 2640 MiB at the demo before it, with the box at 13,950 MiB in use of 16,091; both printed, neither the friendlier reading from earlier in the session. One process, no training, no capacity sweep, no GPU. D_shipped costs 52.2 s for both arms and is built once and shared across all 31 controls. FORWARD CHECK ON THE UPCOMING SCRIPT RULES (it.20-36), applying the two questions this round arrived at: is the threshold sensible, and is the arithmetic beside it true. RESULT IS BETTER THAN THIS ROUND'S 0-FOR-3. VERIFIED CORRECT: it.23's sign-lattice floor 2*2^-8 = 0.0078125 < 0.05; it.24's Delta = t_{.975,7}*sd_paired/sqrt(8) with t(0.975,7) = 2.364624, and the formula is anchored because it is a CI half-width given a measured sd; it.31's tanh saturation threshold, tanh(76.246190/4) = tanh(19.0615) = 1.0 EXACTLY in float64 while tanh(19.0365) = 0.99999999999999989, so the quoted value is the precise boundary and not a round number. MARS FOUND A DIRECT CONFLICT BETWEEN THIS ROUND'S OWN LAW AND ITS OWN CLAUSE, AND HE IS RIGHT. The law: 'bind a must-fire to a CONSTRUCTED input' -- which is HOUSE's repair for instance 21, the must-fire that expired when the eighth seed landed and its guarded branch stopped executing. The clause: a control whose reachable set misses the production domain certifies nothing about production. A must-fire bound to a constructed input IS, by construction, a control whose R may miss D. The two rules point in opposite directions and HOUSE wrote one of them while the other was already in the script. THE RECONCILIATION IS MARS'S ROLE TAXONOMY, and it is the right one: a control that EXERCISES AN INSTRUMENT (does the refusal fire when its condition is violated?) legitimately uses constructed inputs, because its job is to reach a branch, not to describe production. A control that CERTIFIES A PROPERTY OF PRODUCTION must enter through the production path. Same mechanism, opposite requirements, and the deciding fact is the role -- which is exactly why the census cannot infer it. Recorded because a rule this round invented is now known to conflict with a rule this round is enforcing, and a reader applying both without the taxonomy gets stuck.

SEED VARIANCE IS COLLAPSING FASTER THAN SAMPLING NOISE ALONE PREDICTS. SELF-STRIKE, AND IT REVEALS A SCOPE LIMIT IN THE GUARD. HOUSE kept scale/heldout_control_probe.py so the held-out-control measurement would be re-runnable rather than quoted -- correct -- and shipped it with the report loop AT MODULE LEVEL. Importing it runs three 600-step trainings, roughly two minutes of compute. That is the same defect repaired in it13_mars_binding.py, replay_census.py and p1prime.py earlier in this same round, by this same author. IT SLIPPED THROUGH BECAUSE THE GUARD CANNOT SEE IT: tests/loop/test_no_module_writes_a_file_at_import.py detects filesystem WRITES and ARGV READS, not expensive COMPUTATION, and this probe writes nothing. So a module whose import costs two minutes passes a guard whose own docstring is about import-time side effects. THE GUARD'S SCOPE IS NARROWER THAN ITS NAME -- 'writes a file at import' is exactly what it checks and exactly what it says, so this is not a defect in the guard; it is a gap between what the guard covers and what the reader assumes an import-safety check covers. Repaired: body wrapped in main() under a __main__ guard, module-level control flow now none. Recorded because the same reader who wrote three repairs against this class then added a fourth instance of it one scope over, and the guard going green on the new file is instance 23's mechanism again.

FAILED REPRODUCTION, ATTRIBUTED TO A DEFINITIONAL MISMATCH RATHER THAN AN ERROR, AND RECORDED AS SUCH. MARS's it.18 reports D_resource as '36 preflight args via AST -- a line scan would have found zero'. HOUSE attempted to reproduce across 103 scale/*.py files: a naive line scan for a preflight or require call with a digit on the same line found 24, and an AST walk counting numeric or computed arguments to those calls found 31. NEITHER MATCHES (24 vs zero, 31 vs 36). THE LIKELY REASON IS THAT THE TWO SCANS COUNT DIFFERENT THINGS: D_resource is about the argument VALUES reaching preflight, so 'a line scan would have found zero' plausibly means zero recoverable VALUES -- the arguments are variables and computed expressions, not literals -- while HOUSE counted CALL SITES carrying a digit. VERDICT clean-but-unchecked, NOT struck: a non-matching number obtained by measuring something else is not evidence against the original, and calling it one would be the fifth inherited-claim failure inverted -- rejecting a claim on a reproduction that does not target it. The precise definition of D_resource's count is a question for MARS, not a finding against him.

THE VERDICT SPLITS IN TWO AND ONLY ONE HALF IS ROBUST -- stated because the obvious framing is wrong. THE CROSSING IS ROBUST: n=32768 reads CI [1.000851, 1.005679] and n=49152 reads [0.99753, 0.99993], both at threads=12, so the cross-thread systematic offset CANCELS IN THE COMPARISON and the 0.0045 difference is far above any drift. t*=32 genuinely improves between those rungs. THE ABSOLUTE VERDICT IS NOT ROBUST TO THREAD COUNT: the margin below the bar is 7.00e-05 and the measured cross-thread drift is up to 2.345e-03, 33x LARGER -- re-running at threads=6 or 8 could flip LEARNABLE to NOT LEARNABLE. A CATEGORY ERROR HOUSE NEARLY COMMITTED: comparing 7e-5 against 2.345e-3 as though they were the same kind of uncertainty. They are not. At FIXED threads the drift is a systematic offset moving all eight seeds together, not random error on their mean, so the seed CI is the right uncertainty for the mean AND the whole result still sits on a thread-count-dependent baseline. Both cells ran entirely at threads=12, verified via thread_split, which is what makes the comparison valid and the absolute reading fragile.

THE REFUSED EXPERIMENT TURNED OUT TO BE THE WRONG ONE, WHICH IS THE GATE EARNING MORE THAN IT WAS BUILT FOR. scale/vram_gate.py refused the it.10 octave at n=65536 -- 9,859 MiB needed against 8,808 available -- and later measurement showed that figure was itself 8.2% low, so the true requirement is ~11,115 MiB with margin and it would be refused on the now-free box too (8,294 MiB available). THE SUBSTITUTE ANSWERED THE QUESTION BETTER. n=49152 cost less, sat 0.7% above JUPITER's predicted crossing n* = 48,823, and BRACKETED the crossing: n=32768 CI [1.000851, 1.005679] entirely above, n=49152 CI [0.997535, 0.999930] entirely below. The octave would have confirmed further improvement without locating anything, because a cell beyond a crossing does not bracket it. SO THE REFUSAL COST NOTHING AND THE CONSTRAINT IMPROVED THE EXPERIMENT: being unable to afford the obvious cell forced a search for an affordable one, and the affordable one was better aimed. Recorded because a gate is usually justified by the OOM it prevents, and this one is justified by the experiment it redirected.

THE SAME MECHANISM ERRED BOTH WAYS THIS ROUND, AND ONLY ONE DIRECTION IS DANGEROUS. Instance 22: a host-RSS fit measured at n <= 32768 was applied at n = 65536 and understated the requirement by 8.2% -- PERMISSIVE, and it would have let a job through that could not fit had the box had 10 GiB. Symmetrically: HOUSE predicted the n=49152 seed CI would be ~0.005 wide and therefore too marginal to separate JUPITER's two readings, by using the n=32768 SD to estimate an interval at a different rung. The actual CI came in at 0.0024 -- seed variance fell 2.08x where 1/sqrt(n) predicts 1.22x -- and it DID separate them, refuting the deceleration reading. CONSERVATIVE, and it cost nothing but a hedge that turned out unnecessary. BOTH ARE 'A PARAMETER MEASURED AT ONE RUNG APPLIED TO ANOTHER'. The asymmetry is the lesson: an under-estimate of COST admits work that cannot run, while an over-estimate of UNCERTAINTY only means being surprised to have an answer. When extrapolating a parameter out of its measured range, the question is not just 'how wrong might this be' but 'which direction does wrong hurt', and the two deserve different margins.

SECOND FRONTIER PREDICTION UNDER TEST, using the box freed by the t*=32 run. JUPITER's it.10 fit produced TWO crossing predictions and only one has been tested. t*=32 at n* = 48,823 was tested at n=49152 and CONFIRMED -- the crossing is bracketed by CI [1.000851, 1.005679] at n=32768 and [0.997535, 0.999930] at n=49152. The untested one is t*=8 at n* = 16,238, INTERPOLATED (not extrapolated) between measured n=8192 at 1.025127 and n=32768 at 0.974218. Running n=16384, which sits 0.9% above it, at N=8 seeds and threads=12 to match the other cells so the comparison carries no cross-thread offset. GATE: preflight passed at an estimated 2,471 MiB x 1.25 = 3,089 against 8,463 available. NOTE ON THE ESTIMATE, because this round struck itself for the opposite case: n=16384 lies INSIDE the RSS fit's measured range (8192..32768), so this is an interpolation and the 8.2% under-estimate observed BEYOND the range does not apply here. WHAT IT TESTS: an interpolated prediction should be more reliable than the extrapolated one that already landed. If it does NOT land, the frontier fit is worse at interpolation than extrapolation, which would be a strange and important result about the fit rather than about the architecture.

A NATURAL THEORY OF THE CROSSING POINT OVER-PREDICTS BY ~6x, WHICH IS MORE INFORMATIVE THAN A FIT THROUGH THREE POINTS. The 1-hop ceiling is sqrt((t*-1)/t*), so the margin available under the bar is 1 - ceiling, which goes 0.2929 / 0.0646 / 0.0157 at t* = 2 / 8 / 32 and behaves as ~1/(2t*) for large t*. If the crossing were set by RESOLVING that shrinking margin at fixed noise, n ~ 1/m^2 ~ 4t*^2, so t* x4 should cost n* x16. MEASURED: t*=8 crosses near 16,238 (predicted, under test) and t*=32 crosses in (32768, 49152] -- a factor of ~2.5 for the same x4 in t*, against a predicted 16. WHAT THAT SUGGESTS: softmax's difficulty at large t* is NOT primarily margin-resolution. If it were, the data requirement would grow quadratically and it does not. Something else sets the crossing, and the round has not identified it. STATED AS AN OBSERVATION, NOT A LAW: there are three points, one of which (t*=2) is only an UPPER BOUND at n* < 2048 since the smallest rung already reads 0.9523, and one of which (t*=8) is a prediction currently under test at n=16384. Two usable points and a bound do not support a fit, and they do not support a refutation of the theory either -- they support noticing that the two disagree by 6x and saying so.

FIRST SEED AT t*=8, n=16384 READS 0.989218 -- BELOW THE BAR BY 0.0108, which is 4.6x the 2.345e-3 noise floor and therefore not marginal. IT MAY BE A FINDING ABOUT THE FIT RATHER THAN THE ARCHITECTURE. The three cells now read: n=8192 1.025127 (1 seed), n=16384 0.989218 (seed 0), n=32768 0.9754 (8 seeds). The drop is 0.0359 over the FIRST octave and 0.0138 over the SECOND -- the curve is CONVEX in log2(n), steep early and flattening. JUPITER's n* = 16,238 was interpolated across the FULL TWO-OCTAVE GAP, which averages that curvature away; interpolating within the octave that actually contains the crossing puts it nearer n = 13,300. IF THAT SURVIVES EIGHT SEEDS, THE INTERPOLATED PREDICTION IS LESS ACCURATE THAN THE EXTRAPOLATED ONE -- which is the outcome flagged as strange-and-important when this cell was dispatched. The mechanism would be that the interpolation spanned a gap wide enough to hide curvature while the extrapolation sat on a locally linear stretch, so gap WIDTH matters more than interpolation-versus-extrapolation. NOT CONCLUDED: one seed here, and the n=8192 endpoint the whole comparison rests on is itself a SINGLE DRAW. This round has measured twice what a single draw is worth at a marginal cell.

THIS ROUND'S THREAD-DRIFT MEASUREMENT IS THE NUMBER PHASE 2 it.38 WILL NEED. PHASE2_CONTRACT_V_MAIN_4.md item 38 already calls for a 'journals replay check at pinned thread count' -- the contract anticipated that thread count matters. This round measured HOW MUCH: the harness is deterministic given (seed, threads) and NOT across thread counts, with drift up to 2.345e-03 measured over three cross-thread pairs (t*=2 2.345e-3, t*=8 4.911e-4, t*=32 7.311e-6, max is the figure to use). CONSEQUENCES FOR it.38 AND FOR ANY REPLAY: (1) a replay at a different thread count than the original CANNOT reproduce bitwise and should not be scored as though it could; L-VALUE's 5e-7 tolerance is 4,690x tighter than the drift. (2) The pinned count must be RECORDED PER ROW, not per run -- this round's own grid was swept at mixed counts (8, 6, 6, 12, 12) and only the per-cell `threads` field made that visible. (3) Where a verdict's margin is smaller than the drift, the verdict is thread-count-dependent and must say so: t*=32 at n=49152 clears the bar by 7.00e-05 against a possible 2.345e-03 shift, 33x larger. The CROSSING survives because both cells ran at threads=12 and the offset cancels in the comparison; the ABSOLUTE reading does not. Recorded here so it.38 inherits the number rather than re-deriving it.

MEASURED, seed 0 declared pre-run, 20000 MC trials: d=256,k=16 reads 0.174795 [0.174460,0.175131], reproducing the published cell exactly; d=16,k=8 reads 0.547180 [0.545987,0.548373], 3.130x, CIs disjoint by 0.371; shipped key directions read 0.719784 [0.698242,0.741325], 4.12x, because real keys are correlated and so MORE coherent than random. THREE INDEPENDENT FAILURES, so no single repair covers it: (1) wrong width, above; (2) wrong quantity -- the scramble control's residual is |delta ||k|| | in key-norm units and coherence is a dimensionless cosine, so no unit conversion carries one to the other (MATHEMATICS.md:849-853 says 'overlap', correctly; the script line's apposition is where a cosine became a residual); (3) the k<=d premise fails at two of the three shipped k -- --ks defaults to [8,32,128] against d=16, and Welch is exactly 0 only at k<=d, reading welch(16,32)=0.179605 and welch(16,128)=0.234772. THE TELL: welch(16,32)=0.179605 sits within 2.7% of the published 0.174795 while sharing no argument, and five distinct quantities in this repo read within 15% of 0.175, including ceq/diagnose.py:15's content_conditional_sign_decay at s=8 (0.17480). Filed as R10_MECHANISM.md instance 25, reader-side: the instrument states its scope at :18 and claims no transfer. CORRECTION TO THE PRIOR RECORD: 0.1748 was never a cited constant. The v11.1 amendment's figure is 0.147 (mu_jl(256,16)=0.147176); 0.174795 is this repo's own prior measurement, which refuted it. And progress.md:454 prices mu_jl as '15.8% low', an accuracy error. mu_jl and mu_pairs are UNION BOUNDS on E[max], so a valid one must sit ABOVE the measurement; 0.147176 sits BELOW 0.174795 and is therefore not a bound at all. The corrected mu_pairs=0.193397 sits 10.6% above, which is union-bound slack and the correct sign. It is a validity error, and the percentage disguises it. SMALLEST AMENDMENT: print the closed form per row rather than the evaluated constant, so a row cannot be lifted without its arguments; replace the d=256 cell with the measured d=16,k=8 figures; split the coherence sentence from the residual sentence. Bound at scale/r10_it20_coherence.py, whose demo() must-fires on the two dimensions' CIs being disjoint.
